FILE: .devcontainer/features/ladybird/install-ubuntu.sh
#!/bin/sh
set -e

### Check distro
if [ ! -f /etc/lsb-release ]; then
    echo "SCRIPT ERROR: Not an Ubuntu container"
    exit 1
fi

# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. /etc/lsb-release

### Declare helper functions

install_llvm_key() {
    wget -O /usr/share/keyrings/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key
    echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key] http://apt.llvm.org/${DISTRIB_CODENAME}/ llvm-toolchain-${DISTRIB_CODENAME} main" | tee -a /etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm.list
    if [ ! "${LLVM_VERSION}" = "trunk" ]; then
        echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key] http://apt.llvm.org/${DISTRIB_CODENAME}/ llvm-toolchain-${DISTRIB_CODENAME}-${LLVM_VERSION} main" | tee -a /etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm.list
    fi
    apt update -y
}

install_cmake() {
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc 2>/dev/null | gpg --dearmor - | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null
    echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ $(lsb_release -sc) main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list
    apt update -y
    apt install -y cmake
}

### Install packages

apt update -y
apt install -y autoconf autoconf-archive automake build-essential ccache curl fonts-liberation2 git glslang-tools libdrm-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libncurses-dev libpulse-dev libtool libwayland-dev libxcb-icccm4-dev lsb-release nasm ninja-build pkg-config python3 qt6-base-dev qt6-positioning-dev qt6-tools-dev-tools qt6-wayland shellcheck tar unzip zip

install_cmake

### Ensure new enough host compiler is available

VERSION="0.0.0"
if command -v clang >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    VERSION="$(clang -dumpversion)"
fi
MAJOR_VERSION="${VERSION%%.*}"

if [ "${LLVM_VERSION}" = "trunk" ]; then
    install_llvm_key

    apt install -y llvm clang clangd clang-tools lld lldb clang-tidy clang-format
elif [ "${MAJOR_VERSION}" -lt "${LLVM_VERSION}" ]; then
    FAILED_INSTALL=0
    apt install -y "llvm-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clangd-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-tools-${LLVM_VERSION}" "lld-${LLVM_VERSION}" "lldb-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-tidy-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-format-${LLVM_VERSION}"  || FAILED_INSTALL=1

    if [ "${FAILED_INSTALL}" -ne 0 ]; then
        install_llvm_key
        apt install -y "llvm-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clangd-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-tools-${LLVM_VERSION}" "lld-${LLVM_VERSION}" "lldb-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-tidy-${LLVM_VERSION}" "clang-format-${LLVM_VERSION}"
    fi
fi

FILE: .devcontainer/features/vcpkg-cache/install.sh
#!/bin/sh
# Prebuild ladybird's vcpkg dependencies
set -e

# FIXME: Add some options to make this more flexible and usable by other projects
# FIXME: Find a way to do this without cloning ladybird

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64|x64)
      export VCPKG_DEFAULT_TRIPLET=x64-linux-dynamic
      ;;
    aarch64|arm64)
      export VCPKG_DEFAULT_TRIPLET=arm64-linux-dynamic
      export VCPKG_FORCE_SYSTEM_BINARIES=1
      ;;
    *)
      export VCPKG_FORCE_SYSTEM_BINARIES=1
      ;;
esac

cd /tmp

CACHE_DIR=/usr/local/share/vcpkg-binary-cache
mkdir -p ${CACHE_DIR}

# Clone ladybird to get access to vcpkg.json and vcpkg commit id
git clone https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird.git --depth 1
cd ladybird

# Install the vcpkg.json in manifest mode from the root of the repo
# Set the binary cache directory to the one we intend to use at container runtime
export VCPKG_BINARY_SOURCES="clear;files,${CACHE_DIR},readwrite"
export X_VCPKG_ASSET_SOURCES="clear;x-azurl,https://vcpkg-assets.ladybird.org/source-assets/,,read"

install_vcpkg()
{
    preset="${1}"
    preset_lower="$(echo "${preset}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"

    ./Meta/ladybird.py vcpkg --preset "${preset}"
    "./Build/vcpkg-${preset_lower}/vcpkg" install --overlay-triplets="${PWD}/Meta/CMake/vcpkg/${preset_lower}-triplets"
}

# Check options to see which versions we should build
if [ "${RELEASE_TRIPLET}" = "true" ]; then
    install_vcpkg Release
fi
if [ "${DEBUG_TRIPLET}" = "true" ]; then
    install_vcpkg Debug
fi
if [ "${SANITIZER_TRIPLET}" = "true" ]; then
    install_vcpkg Sanitizer
fi

# Clean up to reduce layer size
cd /tmp
rm -rf ladybird

FILE: .github/actions/build/action.yml
name: 'Build'
description: 'Configures, builds and installs Lagom into Build/ and Install/'
author: 'Ladybird'

inputs:
  os:
    description: 'Operating System to build for'
    required: true
  arch:
    description: 'Target Architecture to build for'
    required: true
  toolchain:
    description: 'Toolchain to build with'
    required: true
  build_preset:
    description: 'CMake preset to configure with'
    required: true
  clang_plugins:
    description: 'Whether to build with the Clang plugins'
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  version:
    description: 'Version of a release build, if any'
    required: false
    default: ''
  use_caches:
    description: 'Whether to restore and save caches of downloaded files and build artifacts'
    required: false
    default: 'true'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Set Up Environment
      uses: $/.github/actions/setup
      id: 'setup'
      with:
        os: ${{ inputs.os }}
        arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
        toolchain: ${{ inputs.toolchain }}
        build_preset: ${{ inputs.build_preset }}
        use_caches: ${{ inputs.use_caches }}

    # Use the compiler version for the ccache compiler hash. Otherwise, if plugins are enabled, the plugin .so files
    # are included in the hash. This results in clean builds on every run as the .so files are rebuilt.
    #
    # Note: This only works because our plugins do not transform any code. If that becomes untrue, we must revisit this.
    - name: Set the ccache compiler check
      shell: bash
      run: echo "CCACHE_COMPILERCHECK=%compiler% -v" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

    # === PREPARE FOR BUILDING ===

    - name: Assign Build Parameters
      if: ${{ inputs.os != 'Windows' }}
      id: 'build-parameters'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        CMAKE_OPTIONS="-DLADYBIRD_BASELINE_CPU_TARGET=ON"
        if ${{ inputs.os == 'Linux' }} ; then
          if ${{ inputs.build_preset == 'Distribution' }} && [[ -r /etc/os-release ]]; then
            # shellcheck source=/dev/null
            . /etc/os-release

            # Ubuntu 26.04 is the first release with Qt 6.10 or newer.
            if [[ "${ID:-}" == 'ubuntu' && -n "${VERSION_ID:-}" ]] && dpkg --compare-versions "$VERSION_ID" lt 26; then
              CMAKE_OPTIONS="$CMAKE_OPTIONS -DLADYBIRD_BUILD_QT=ON"
            fi
          fi

          # FIXME: https://github.com/WebAssembly/wabt/issues/2533
          #        wabt doesn't have binary releases for arm64 Linux
          if ${{ inputs.arch == 'arm64' }} ; then
            PKGCONFIG=$(which pkg-config)
            CMAKE_OPTIONS="$CMAKE_OPTIONS -DPKG_CONFIG_EXECUTABLE=$PKGCONFIG"
          fi

          if ${{ inputs.toolchain == 'Clang' }} ; then
            echo "host_cc=clang" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "host_cxx=clang++" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif ${{ inputs.toolchain == 'GNU' }} ; then
            echo "host_cc=gcc" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "host_cxx=g++" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
        elif ${{ inputs.os == 'macOS' }} ; then
          echo "host_cc=$(xcrun --find clang)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "host_cxx=$(xcrun --find clang++)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        fi

        if ${{ inputs.clang_plugins == 'true' }} ; then
          echo "ccache_key=${{ inputs.build_preset }}-CLANG_PLUGINS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          CMAKE_OPTIONS="$CMAKE_OPTIONS -DENABLE_CLANG_PLUGINS=ON"
        else
          echo "ccache_key=${{ inputs.build_preset }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          CMAKE_OPTIONS="$CMAKE_OPTIONS -DINCLUDE_WASM_SPEC_TESTS=ON -DWASM_SPEC_TEST_SKIP_FORMATTING=ON"
        fi

        echo "cmake_options=$CMAKE_OPTIONS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Restore Caches
      if: ${{ inputs.use_caches == 'true' }}
      uses: $/.github/actions/cache-restore
      id: 'cache-restore'
      with:
        os: ${{ inputs.os }}
        arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
        toolchain: ${{ inputs.toolchain }}
        cache_key_extra: ${{ inputs.os == 'Windows' && inputs.build_preset || steps.build-parameters.outputs.ccache_key }}
        ccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.ccache_path }}
        sccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.sccache_path }}
        vcpkg_cache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}

    - name: Restore the WebAssembly spec test suite
      id: 'wasm-spec-tests-cache'
      if: ${{ inputs.use_caches == 'true' && inputs.os != 'Windows' }}
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build/caches/WasmSpecTests
        key: wasm-spec-test-suite | ${{ hashFiles('Meta/CMake/wasm_spec_tests.cmake') }}

    - name: Set dynamic environment variables
      if: ${{ inputs.os != 'Windows' }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        # Note: Required for vcpkg to use this compiler for its own builds.
        echo "CC=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cc }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo "CXX=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cxx }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

    - name: Create Build Environment
      if: ${{ inputs.os != 'Windows' && inputs.build_preset != 'Fuzzers' }}
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      shell: bash
      env:
        RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      run: |
        cmake --preset ${{ inputs.build_preset }} -B Build \
          ${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.cmake_options }} \
          -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=${{ env.pythonLocation }}/bin/python \
          -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cc }} \
          -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cxx }} \
          "-DLADYBIRD_VERSION=${RELEASE_VERSION}"

    - name: Create Build Environment (Windows)
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'Windows' }}
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      shell: pwsh
      run: |
        cmake --preset ${{ inputs.build_preset }} -B Build `
          -DLADYBIRD_BASELINE_CPU_TARGET=ON

    - name: Create Build Environment (Fuzzers)
      if: ${{ inputs.build_preset == 'Fuzzers' }}
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        cmake --preset ${{ inputs.build_preset }} -B Build \
          ${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.cmake_options }} \
          -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=${{ env.pythonLocation }}/bin/python \
          -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cc }} \
          -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cxx }}

    # === BUILD ===

    - name: Build
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build
      shell: bash
      run: cmake --build .

    - name: Install
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build
      shell: bash
      run: cmake --install . --strip --prefix "${{ github.workspace }}/Install"

    - name: Save the WebAssembly spec test suite
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' && inputs.use_caches == 'true' && inputs.os != 'Windows' && steps.wasm-spec-tests-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' }}
      uses: actions/cache/save@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build/caches/WasmSpecTests
        key: ${{ steps.wasm-spec-tests-cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

    - name: Save Caches
      if: ${{ inputs.use_caches == 'true' }}
      uses: $/.github/actions/cache-save
      with:
        arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
        ccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.ccache_path }}
        ccache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.ccache_primary_key }}
        sccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.sccache_path }}
        sccache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.sccache_primary_key }}
        vcpkg_cache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}
        vcpkg_cache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.vcpkg_cache_primary_key }}

FILE: .github/actions/cache-restore/action.yml
name: 'Cache Restore Action'
description: 'Restores caches of downloaded files and build artifacts.'
author: 'Andrew Kaster <akaster@serenityos.org>'

inputs:
  os:
    description: 'Operating System to restore caches for'
    required: true
  arch:
    description: 'Target Architecture to restore caches for'
    required: true
  toolchain:
    description: 'Toolchain to restore caches for (GNU or Clang)'
    required: true
  cache_key_extra:
    description: 'Code coverage setting, ON or OFF, or debug setting, ALL or NORMAL'
    required: true
  ccache_path:
    description: 'Path to the ccache directory'
    required: true
  sccache_path:
    description: 'Path to the sccache directory'
    required: true
  vcpkg_cache_path:
    description: 'Path to vcpkg binary cache'
    required: true

outputs:
  ccache_primary_key:
    description: 'Primary ccache key'
    value: ${{ steps.ccache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
  sccache_primary_key:
    description: 'Primary sccache key'
    value: ${{ steps.sccache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
  vcpkg_cache_primary_key:
    description: 'Primary vcpkg binary cache key, or empty if the cache was restored from an exact key match'
    value: ${{ steps.vcpkg.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' && steps.vcpkg.outputs.cache-primary-key || '' }}

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: 'Date Stamp'
      shell: bash
      id: 'date-stamp'
      run: |
        echo "timestamp=$(date -u "+%Y%m%d%H%M_%S")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: 'Compiler Cache'
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v6.1.0
      id: 'ccache'
      with:
        path: ${{ inputs.ccache_path }}
        key: ccache | ${{ inputs.os }} | ${{ inputs.arch }} | ${{ inputs.toolchain }} | ${{ inputs.cache_key_extra }} | ${{ steps.date-stamp.outputs.timestamp }}
        restore-keys: |
          ccache | ${{ inputs.os }} | ${{ inputs.arch }} | ${{ inputs.toolchain }} | ${{ inputs.cache_key_extra }}

    - name: 'Configure Compiler Cache'
      if: ${{ inputs.os != 'Windows' }}
      shell: bash
      env:
        CCACHE_DIR: ${{ inputs.ccache_path }}
      run: |
          ccache -M 0

          # Reset all ccache modification dates to a known epoch. This provides a baseline that we can prune against.
          find "${{ inputs.ccache_path }}" | tac | xargs touch -a -m -d "2018-10-10T09:53:07Z"

          ccache -s
          ccache -z

    - name: 'Configure Compiler Cache (Windows)'
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'Windows' }}
      shell: pwsh
      env:
        CCACHE_DIR: ${{ inputs.ccache_path }}
      run: |
        ccache -M 0

        # Reset all ccache modification dates to a known epoch. This provides a baseline that we can prune against.
        Get-ChildItem -Path "${{ inputs.ccache_path }}" -Recurse | Sort-Object FullName -Descending | ForEach-Object {
            $_.LastWriteTime = [DateTime]::Parse("2018-10-10T09:53:07Z")
            $_.LastAccessTime = [DateTime]::Parse("2018-10-10T09:53:07Z")
        }

        ccache -s
        ccache -z

    - name: 'Rust Compiler Cache'
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v6.1.0
      id: 'sccache'
      with:
        path: ${{ inputs.sccache_path }}
        key: sccache | ${{ inputs.os }} | ${{ inputs.arch }} | ${{ inputs.toolchain }} | ${{ inputs.cache_key_extra }} | ${{ steps.date-stamp.outputs.timestamp }}
        restore-keys: |
          sccache | ${{ inputs.os }} | ${{ inputs.arch }} | ${{ inputs.toolchain }} | ${{ inputs.cache_key_extra }}

    - name: 'Restore vcpkg cache'
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v6.1.0
      id: 'vcpkg'
      with:
        path: ${{ inputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}
        key: vcpkg | ${{ inputs.os }} | ${{ inputs.arch }} | ${{ inputs.toolchain }} | ${{ inputs.cache_key_extra }} | ${{ hashFiles('vcpkg.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          vcpkg | ${{ inputs.os }} | ${{ inputs.arch }} | ${{ inputs.toolchain }} | ${{ inputs.cache_key_extra }}

FILE: .github/actions/cache-save/action.yml
name: 'Cache Save Action'
description: 'Saves caches of build artifacts.'
author: 'Andrew Kaster <akaster@serenityos.org>'

inputs:
  arch:
    description: 'Target Architecture to restore caches for'
    required: true
  ccache_path:
    description: 'Path to the ccache directory'
    required: true
  ccache_primary_key:
    description: 'Primary ccache key'
    required: true
  sccache_path:
    description: 'Path to the sccache directory'
    required: true
  sccache_primary_key:
    description: 'Primary sccache key'
    required: true
  vcpkg_cache_path:
    description: 'Path to the vcpkg binary cache directory'
    required: true
  vcpkg_cache_primary_key:
    description: 'Primary vcpkg binary cache key, or empty to skip saving the vcpkg binary cache'
    required: true

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: 'Prune obsolete ccache files'
      shell: bash
      env:
        CCACHE_DIR: ${{ inputs.ccache_path }}
      run: |
        ccache --evict-older-than=1d

    - name: 'Compiler Cache'
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
      uses: actions/cache/save@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ${{ inputs.ccache_path }}
        key: ${{ inputs.ccache_primary_key }}

    - name: 'Cache Stats'
      shell: bash
      env:
        CCACHE_DIR: ${{ inputs.ccache_path }}
      run: |
        ccache -s

    # Stopping the server gives its in-flight requests up to 10 seconds to finish, and prints the stats for the job's
    # Rust compiles. It isn't running if nothing invoked it, or on Windows, where it doesn't outlive the build step.
    - name: 'Stop the Rust compiler cache server'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        sccache --stop-server || true

    - name: 'Rust Compiler Cache'
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
      uses: actions/cache/save@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ${{ inputs.sccache_path }}
        key: ${{ inputs.sccache_primary_key }}

    - name: 'vcpkg binary cache'
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' && inputs.vcpkg_cache_primary_key != '' }}
      uses: actions/cache/save@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ${{ inputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}
        key: ${{ inputs.vcpkg_cache_primary_key }}

FILE: .github/actions/setup/action.yml
name: 'Setup action'
description: 'Sets up shared CI tooling'
author: 'Andrew Kaster <akaster@serenityos.org>'
inputs:
  os:
    description: 'Operating System to set up'
    required: true
    default: 'Linux'
  arch:
    description: 'Target Architecture to set up'
    required: true
    default: 'x86_64'
  toolchain:
    description: 'Toolchain to use'
    required: true
    default: 'Clang'
  type:
    description: 'Whether the setup is for building or linting'
    required: false
    default: 'build'
  build_preset:
    description: 'When the setup is for building, set the build preset (e.g. Release)'
    required: false
    default: 'Release'
  use_caches:
    description: 'Whether to restore and save caches of downloaded files'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
outputs:
  ccache_path:
    description: 'Path to the ccache directory'
    value: ${{ steps.workspace.outputs.ccache_path }}
  sccache_path:
    description: 'Path to the sccache directory'
    value: ${{ steps.workspace.outputs.sccache_path }}
  vcpkg_cache_path:
    description: 'Path to the vcpkg binary cache'
    value: ${{ steps.workspace.outputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: 'Set workspace environment'
      id: 'workspace'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        echo "LADYBIRD_SOURCE_DIR=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo "CCACHE_DIR=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo "ccache_path=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.ccache" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "SCCACHE_DIR=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.sccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo "SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=2G" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo "SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo "sccache_path=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.sccache" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "vcpkg_cache_path=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Build/caches/vcpkg-binary-cache" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=${RUNNER_TEMP}/gitconfig" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        git config --file "${RUNNER_TEMP}/gitconfig" --add safe.directory "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}"
        mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/pip-cache"
        echo "PIP_CACHE_DIR=${RUNNER_TEMP}/pip-cache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

    - uses: actions/setup-python@v7.1.0
      if: ${{ inputs.os != 'Linux' }}
      with:
        python-version: 3.12
        cache: ${{ inputs.use_caches == 'true' && 'pip' || '' }}
        cache-dependency-path: requirements.txt

    # Use the system interpreter in Linux job containers: actions/setup-python can
    # fail to find its tool-cache pip there.
    - name: 'Set up Python environment'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        python_bin=$(python3 "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Meta/Utils/python_environment.py" --print-bin | tr -d '\r')
        echo "${python_bin}" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        echo "pythonLocation=$(dirname "${python_bin}")" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

    - name: 'Select latest Xcode'
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'macOS' }}
      uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1.7.0
      with:
        xcode-version: '27'

    - name: 'Install Dependencies'
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'macOS' }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        brew update

        brew unlink openssl@3 || true

        brew install \
            autoconf \
            autoconf-archive \
            automake \
            bash \
            ccache \
            coreutils \
            libtool \
            nasm \
            ninja \
            pkg-config \
            sccache \
            unzip

    - name: 'Install Dependencies'
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'Windows' }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        choco install -y sccache --no-progress

        if ! where clang-cl > /dev/null 2>&1 ; then
          # Keep the LLVM version in sync with GitHub's Windows runner image:
          # https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/windows/Windows2025-Readme.md
          choco install -y llvm --no-progress --version=20.1.8

          echo "C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"
          export PATH="/c/Program Files/LLVM/bin:${PATH}"
        fi
        clang-cl --version

    - name: 'Put rustup on the PATH'
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'macOS' }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        if command -v rustup > /dev/null 2>&1 ; then
          exit 0
        fi

        # The self-hosted macOS runners have rustup installed in the cargo home, but not on their PATH.
        CARGO_BIN="${CARGO_HOME:-${HOME}/.cargo}/bin"
        if [ ! -x "${CARGO_BIN}/rustup" ]; then
          echo "rustup is neither on the PATH nor in ${CARGO_BIN}; install it on this runner" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "${CARGO_BIN}" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"

    - name: 'Warm up the Rust toolchain'
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'macOS' || inputs.os == 'Windows' }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        if rustup toolchain install && cargo --version && rustc --version ; then
          exit 0
        fi

        # Some Blacksmith runner images boot with a partially installed toolchain. Either it has files rustup doesn't
        # know about, which rustup can't repair on its own and fails on with a "detected conflict" error, or it lacks
        # cargo or rustc although rustup reports the toolchain as installed. So wipe the toolchain and retry.
        CHANNEL=$(sed -n 's/^channel *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p' "${{ github.workspace }}/rust-toolchain.toml")
        if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then
          echo "Could not determine the pinned Rust channel" >&2
          exit 1
        fi

        echo "Reinstalling Rust toolchain ${CHANNEL} from scratch"
        rustup toolchain uninstall "${CHANNEL}" || rm -rf "$(rustup show home)/toolchains/${CHANNEL}"-*
        rustup toolchain install
        cargo --version
        rustc --version

    - name: 'Resolve wasm-tools release'
      id: 'wasm-tools'
      if: ${{ inputs.type == 'build' && inputs.os != 'Linux' }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        VERSION=1.243.0
        if ${{ inputs.arch == 'arm64' }} ; then
          ARCH=aarch64
        else
          ARCH=${{ inputs.arch }}
        fi
        LOWERCASE_OS=$( echo -n '${{ inputs.os }}' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
        if ${{ inputs.os == 'Windows' }} ; then
          EXTENSION=zip
        else
          EXTENSION=tar.gz
        fi
        NAME="wasm-tools-${VERSION}-${ARCH}-${LOWERCASE_OS}"
        echo "version=${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "name=${NAME}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "filename=${NAME}.${EXTENSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "extension=${EXTENSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: 'Restore wasm-tools'
      id: 'wasm-tools-cache'
      if: ${{ inputs.use_caches == 'true' && inputs.type == 'build' && inputs.os != 'Linux' }}
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ${{ github.workspace }}/wasm-tools
        key: ${{ steps.wasm-tools.outputs.name }}

    - name: 'Install wasm-tools'
      if: ${{ inputs.type == 'build' && inputs.os != 'Linux' && steps.wasm-tools-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' }}
      shell: bash
      run: |
        FILENAME="${{ steps.wasm-tools.outputs.filename }}"
        URL="https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasm-tools/releases/download/v${{ steps.wasm-tools.outputs.version }}/${FILENAME}"

        delays=(5 15 45)
        attempt=1
        until curl --fail --location --output "${FILENAME}" "${URL}"; do
          if (( attempt > ${#delays[@]} )); then
            echo "wasm-tools download failed after $(( ${#delays[@]} + 1 )) attempts" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "wasm-tools download failed; retrying in ${delays[attempt-1]}s" >&2
          sleep "${delays[attempt-1]}"
          attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
        done

        if [ "${{ steps.wasm-tools.outputs.extension }}" == 'zip' ]; then
          unzip "${FILENAME}"
        else
          tar -xzf "${FILENAME}"
        fi
        rm "${FILENAME}"
        mv "${{ steps.wasm-tools.outputs.name }}" wasm-tools

    # Saved right after the install rather than by actions/cache's post-job step, which runs only if the whole job
    # succeeds — so a flaky test would keep the cache from ever being saved.
    - name: 'Save wasm-tools'
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' && inputs.use_caches == 'true' && inputs.type == 'build' && inputs.os != 'Linux' && steps.wasm-tools-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' }}
      uses: actions/cache/save@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ${{ github.workspace }}/wasm-tools
        key: ${{ steps.wasm-tools-cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

    - name: 'Add wasm-tools to PATH'
      if: ${{ inputs.type == 'build' && inputs.os != 'Linux' }}
      shell: bash
      run: echo "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/wasm-tools" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

    - name: 'Restore cargo registry'
      id: 'cargo-registry'
      if: ${{ inputs.use_caches == 'true' }}
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          /opt/cargo/registry
        key: cargo-registry-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock', 'Libraries/LibJS/Flap/Cargo.lock') }}
        restore-keys: |
          cargo-registry-${{ runner.os }}-

    - name: 'Fetch cargo dependencies'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        # Fetch every crate in both lockfiles, so the registry cache saved after this step is complete no matter
        # which job saves it first, or which crates that job builds. Builds of older commits run this action from
        # master, so skip any manifest that the checkout doesn't have.
        for manifest in Cargo.toml Libraries/LibJS/Flap/Cargo.toml; do
          if [ -f "${manifest}" ]; then
            cargo fetch --locked --manifest-path "${manifest}"
          fi
        done

    # Saved right after the fetch rather than by actions/cache's post-job step, which runs only if the whole job
    # succeeds — so a flaky test would keep the cache from ever being saved.
    - name: 'Save cargo registry'
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' && inputs.use_caches == 'true' && steps.cargo-registry.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' }}
      uses: actions/cache/save@v6.1.0
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          /opt/cargo/registry
        key: ${{ steps.cargo-registry.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

    - name: 'Set required environment variables'
      if: ${{ inputs.os == 'Linux' && inputs.arch == 'arm64' }}
      shell: bash
      run: echo "VCPKG_FORCE_SYSTEM_BINARIES=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

    - name: 'Install vcpkg'
      if: ${{ inputs.type == 'build' }}
      shell: bash
      run: ./Meta/ladybird.py vcpkg --preset "${{ inputs.build_preset }}"

FILE: .github/workflows/backport-labels.yml
name: Backport labels

on:
  create:

jobs:
  create-label:
    if: >-
      github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
      && github.ref_type == 'branch'
      && startsWith(github.ref_name, 'release/')
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404

    permissions:
      issues: write

    steps:
      - name: 'Create the label for backporting to the new release branch'
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          gh label create "backport ${BRANCH#release/}" --repo "$REPO" --force --color 0e8a16 \
            --description "Backport to ${BRANCH} once merged"

================================================================================
FILE: .github/workflows/backport.yml
name: Backport

# Labeling a PR to master with `backport 2026.46` cherry-picks its commits onto release/2026.46 once it is merged, or
# right away if it already is, with `git cherry-pick -x`, and opens a PR against that release branch from a branch named
# `backport/<PR>-to-<release branch>`, titled `[Backport <release branch>] <PR title>`. These PRs are opened by a bot,
# not by whoever added the label, and run CI like any other PR. A cherry-pick that conflicts still gets a PR, as a draft
# with the conflict committed; resolve it on that PR's branch. The original PR gets a comment with the outcome. The
# `no backport` label records that a PR shouldn't be backported, and removing it backports to the PR's backport labels.
# The backport branch is deleted when its PR is closed without being merged; GitHub deletes it on merge.

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [closed, labeled, unlabeled]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
  queue: max

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: >-
      github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
      && github.event.pull_request.merged
      && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == 'master'
      && contains(toJSON(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name), '"backport ')
      && (github.event.action == 'closed'
        || (github.event.action == 'labeled'
          && (startsWith(github.event.label.name, 'backport ') || github.event.label.name == 'no backport'))
        || (github.event.action == 'unlabeled' && github.event.label.name == 'no backport'))
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404

    permissions:
      pull-requests: write

    outputs:
      branches: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.branches }}

    steps:
      - name: 'Check who asked, and for which release branches'
        id: parse
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          SENDER: ${{ github.event.sender.login }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          ADDED_LABEL: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
          LABELS: ${{ toJSON(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name) }}
        run: |
          mapfile -t backport_labels < <(jq -r '.[] | select(startswith("backport "))' <<< "$LABELS")
          problems=()
          problem() {
            echo "::error::$*"
            problems+=("$*")
          }

          branches=()
          permission=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/collaborators/${SENDER}/permission" --jq .permission)
          if jq -e 'index("no backport")' <<< "$LABELS" > /dev/null; then
            listed=$(printf "\`%s\`, " "${backport_labels[@]}")
            problem "This PR is labeled both \`no backport\` and ${listed%, }." \
              "Remove \`no backport\` to backport it, or the backport labels if it shouldn't be backported."
          elif ! [[ "$permission" =~ ^(admin|maintain|write)$ ]]; then
            problem "Backports need write access to this repository, which ${SENDER} doesn't have." \
              "Someone with write access can remove and re-add the backport labels."
          else
            if [ "$ACTION" = labeled ]; then
              # The release branches that the PR was already labeled for got their backports when it was merged.
              backport_labels=("$ADDED_LABEL")
            fi
            for label in "${backport_labels[@]}"; do
              version="${label#backport }"
              if ! [[ "$version" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
                problem "\`${label}\` doesn't name a release, such as \`backport 2026.46\`." \
                  "Replace it with the label of the release to backport to."
                continue
              fi
              branch="release/${version}"
              if ! gh api "repos/${REPO}/branches/${branch}" --silent 2> /dev/null; then
                problem "\`${branch}\` doesn't exist, so there is nothing to backport to for \`${label}\`." \
                  "Remove the label."
                continue
              fi
              head="backport/${PR}-to-${branch}"
              if lookup=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/branches/${head}" --silent 2>&1); then
                open_prs=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls?state=open&head=${REPO%%/*}:${head}&base=${branch}" --jq length)
                if [ "$open_prs" -eq 0 ]; then
                  problem "\`${head}\` is left over from a closed backport PR." \
                    "Delete that branch, then remove and re-add \`${label}\`."
                  continue
                fi
              elif [[ "$lookup" != *"(HTTP 404)"* ]]; then
                problem "Couldn't check whether \`${head}\` exists (${lookup})." \
                  "Remove and re-add \`${label}\` to try again."
                continue
              fi
              branches+=("$branch")
            done
          fi

          echo "branches=${branches[*]}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "${#branches[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "Backporting #${PR} to ${branches[*]}, for ${SENDER}." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          if [ "${#problems[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            {
              echo "Some of the backports that this PR's labels ask for can't start:"
              echo
              printf -- '- %s\n' "${problems[@]}"
            } > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/problems.md"
            gh api "repos/${REPO}/issues/${PR}/comments" -F "body=@${RUNNER_TEMP}/problems.md" --silent
            exit 1
          fi

  delete-branch:
    if: >-
      github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
      && github.event.action == 'closed'
      && !github.event.pull_request.merged
      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
      && startsWith(github.event.pull_request.base.ref, 'release/')
      && startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'backport/')
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404

    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: 'Delete the backport branch'
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        run: |
          open_prs=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls?state=open&head=${REPO%%/*}:${HEAD}" --jq length)
          if [ "$open_prs" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "An open PR uses ${HEAD}, so the branch stays."
            exit 0
          fi
          if ! output=$(gh api --method DELETE "repos/${REPO}/git/refs/heads/${HEAD}" 2>&1); then
            # Someone may have deleted the branch already.
            lookup=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/branches/${HEAD}" --silent 2>&1) && exists=1 || exists=0
            if [ "$exists" -eq 1 ] || [[ "$lookup" != *"(HTTP 404)"* ]]; then
              echo "::error::$output"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

  backport:
    needs: prepare
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.prepare.outputs.branches != '' }}
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404

    permissions: {}

    steps:
      - name: 'Create a token for the Ladybird Backport app'
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3.4.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.BACKPORT_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.BACKPORT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: 'Checkout ladybird'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

      - name: 'Create the backport PRs'
        id: backport
        uses: korthout/backport-action@v5.0.0
        with:
          github_token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          label_pattern: ''
          target_branches: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.branches }}
          branch_name: backport/${pull_number}-to-${target_branch}
          pull_description: 'Backport of #${pull_number} to `${target_branch}`.'
          auto_merge_enabled: true
          auto_merge_method: rebase
          experimental: '{"conflict_resolution": "draft_commit_conflicts"}'

      - name: 'Fail if any backport failed'
        if: ${{ steps.backport.outputs.was_successful != 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          WAS_SUCCESSFUL_BY_TARGET: ${{ steps.backport.outputs.was_successful_by_target }}
        run: |
          failed=$(sed -n 's/=false$//p' <<< "${WAS_SUCCESSFUL_BY_TARGET}" | paste -sd ' ' -)
          echo "::error::Backporting to ${failed} failed. See the comment on the original PR."
          exit 1

================================================================================
FILE: .github/workflows/bench-pr.yml
name: 'PR benchmarks'

# Measures a PR against its merge-base with web-benchmarks' bench_pr.py, on the web-benchmarks runners, and adds the
# result to the end of the PR's description. Nothing runs on its own: A maintainer either adds the "benchmark" label to
# the PR (the run removes it again when it finishes), or dispatches this workflow with the PR's number.
#
# Both triggers run master's copy of this file, never the PR's. The PR's code is built and run only in the bench jobs,
# which get a read-only token and no secrets; only the report job, which runs nothing from the PR, can write to it.
#
# Every run builds both arms from scratch in its own workspace, and saves nothing to the Actions cache. The one thing
# that outlives a run is each runner's calibration record (bench_pr.py's noise floor, a few hundred bytes), which a
# calibration run uploads as an artifact and later runs download.

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr:
        description: 'PR number (leave empty for a calibration)'
        type: string
        default: ''
      calibrate:
        description: 'Measure master against itself, to record each runner''s noise floor'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      rounds:
        description: 'Measured rounds'
        type: string
        default: '8'
      focus:
        description: 'Suites or tests the change targets, space-separated (bench_pr.py --focus)'
        type: string
        default: ''
      benchmarks:
        description: 'Suites to run, comma-separated (default: all)'
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # One run per PR, so labeling a PR again replaces its run in progress. Every other label starts this workflow too,
  # but in a group of its own — so it never cancels a benchmark run.
  group: >-
    ${{ github.workflow }}-${{
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && (inputs.calibrate && 'calibrate' || inputs.pr)
      || github.event.label.name == 'benchmark' && github.event.pull_request.number
      || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: >-
      github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
      && (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.label.name == 'benchmark')
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404

    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    outputs:
      pr: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.pr }}
      head: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.head }}
      matrix: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.matrix }}

    steps:
      - name: 'Checkout ladybird'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: .github/workflows/ci.yml
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: 'Resolve the PR, and check who asked'
        id: resolve
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REQUESTER: ${{ github.triggering_actor }}
          CALIBRATE: ${{ inputs.calibrate }}
          PR_INPUT: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          ROUNDS: ${{ inputs.rounds }}
          LABELED_PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          LABELED_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          has_write_access() {
            case "$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/collaborators/$1/permission" --jq .permission)" in
              admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
            esac
          }

          # Adding a label takes only triage access, and a re-run counts as asking too.
          if ! has_write_access "$REQUESTER"; then
            echo "::error::Benchmark runs are for maintainers, and ${REQUESTER} has no write access."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "${ROUNDS:-}" ] && ! [[ "$ROUNDS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::rounds must be a number, not '${ROUNDS}'."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [ "$EVENT" = workflow_dispatch ] && [ "$CALIBRATE" = true ]; then
            pr=
            head=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/commits/master" --jq .sha)
          else
            pr=${LABELED_PR:-$PR_INPUT}
            if ! [[ "$pr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Give a PR number, or ask for a calibration."
              exit 1
            fi
            gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls/${pr}" > pr.json
            # A merged PR can be measured too: Its head stays fetchable, and since PRs land only by rebasing, that head
            # never lands on master itself — so its merge-base is still the commit it branched from.
            if ! jq -e '(.state == "open" or .merged_at != null) and .base.ref == "master"' pr.json > /dev/null; then
              echo "::error::#${pr} isn't an open or merged PR against master."
              exit 1
            fi
            # A label run measures the head the PR had when the label went on, so a push after that can't change what
            # gets built.
            head=${LABELED_HEAD:-$(jq -r .head.sha pr.json)}
          fi

          image=$(grep -o 'ghcr.io/ladybirdbrowser/ladybird-ci:[0-9.]*' .github/workflows/ci.yml | head -1)
          if [ -z "$image" ]; then
            echo "::error::No ladybird-ci image named in ci.yml."
            exit 1
          fi
          matrix=$(jq -cn --arg image "$image" '{include: [
            {os_name: "Linux", arch: "x86_64",
             runner_labels: (["ubuntu-24.04-internal", "web-benchmarks", "self-hosted"] | tojson),
             container: ({image: $image, options: "--shm-size=4g"} | tojson)},
            {os_name: "macOS", arch: "arm64",
             runner_labels: (["macos-26", "web-benchmarks", "self-hosted"] | tojson),
             container: "null"}
          ]}')

          {
            echo "pr=${pr}"
            echo "head=${head}"
            echo "matrix=${matrix}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ -n "$pr" ]; then what="#${pr} at ${head}"; else what="${head} against itself"; fi
          echo "Measuring ${what}, for ${REQUESTER}." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  bench:
    needs: prepare
    name: ${{ matrix.os_name }}, ${{ matrix.arch }}
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.runner_labels) }}
    container: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.container) }}
    timeout-minutes: 480

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.prepare.outputs.matrix) }}

    # This job builds and runs the PR's code: a read-only token, and no secrets.
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: 'Checkout ladybird'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: 'Checkout LadybirdBrowser/web-benchmarks'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: LadybirdBrowser/web-benchmarks
          path: web-benchmarks
          ref: master
          persist-credentials: false

      # No caches: This job runs the PR's code, so nothing it leaves behind goes into a cache that other workflows
      # restore.
      - name: 'Set Up Environment'
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup
        with:
          os: ${{ matrix.os_name }}
          arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          toolchain: 'Clang'
          build_preset: 'Distribution'
          use_caches: 'false'

      # A compare run quotes the resolution of the runner's latest calibration on master, which bench_pr.py reads from
      # its cache directory.
      - name: 'Find the latest calibration'
        id: calibration
        if: ${{ !inputs.calibrate }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NAME: bench-pr-noise-floor-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GH_TOKEN}" \
              "${GITHUB_API_URL}/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/artifacts?name=${NAME}&per_page=100" > artifacts.json
          run_id=$(python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json
          artifacts = [a for a in json.load(open("artifacts.json"))["artifacts"]
                       if not a["expired"] and a["workflow_run"]["head_branch"] == "master"
                       and a["workflow_run"]["head_repository_id"] == a["workflow_run"]["repository_id"]]
          print(max(artifacts, key=lambda a: a["created_at"])["workflow_run"]["id"] if artifacts else "")
          EOF
          )
          echo "run_id=${run_id}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: 'Download the latest calibration'
        if: ${{ steps.calibration.outputs.run_id != '' }}
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bench-pr-noise-floor-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          run-id: ${{ steps.calibration.outputs.run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          path: bench-state/cache/ladybird-bench

      - name: 'Run bench_pr.py'
        shell: bash
        env:
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.head }}
          CALIBRATE: ${{ inputs.calibrate }}
          ROUNDS: ${{ inputs.rounds || '8' }}
          FOCUS: ${{ inputs.focus }}
          BENCHMARKS: ${{ inputs.benchmarks }}
          PLATFORM: ${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/bench-state
          # One directory per platform inside the artifact, so the report job finds each platform's files at the same
          # place whether it downloads one artifact or several.
          out=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/bench-pr-out/$PLATFORM
          mkdir -p "$state" "$out"

          # bench_pr.py keeps its worktrees, its logs and the calibration record under XDG_CACHE_HOME. The two arms are
          # two worktrees: Relative paths, with no hashed working directory, make one arm's objects hits for the other.
          export XDG_CACHE_HOME=$state/cache
          export CCACHE_DIR=$state/cache/ccache CCACHE_MAXSIZE=10G
          export CCACHE_BASEDIR=$state/worktrees CCACHE_NOHASHDIR=true
          export SCCACHE_DIR=$state/cache/sccache SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=5G
          # Both arms build with the CI image's clang, as the master runs do.
          [ "$RUNNER_OS" = Linux ] && export CC=clang CXX=clang++
          # The raw results hold each round's timings per arm and suite, which the report summarizes away: They're what
          # it takes to tell a real mover from noise in a test, e.g. a bimodal timing, or a drift across the rounds.
          save_logs_and_raw_results() {
            cp "$XDG_CACHE_HOME"/ladybird-bench/compile-*.log "$out"/ 2> /dev/null || true
            # A compile log names a vcpkg port that failed to build, but the port's own logs hold the error.
            local arm port
            for arm in base head; do
              sed -n 's/^error: building \([^:[]*\).*/\1/p' "$XDG_CACHE_HOME/ladybird-bench/compile-$arm.log" 2> /dev/null \
                | sort -u | while read -r port; do
                  mkdir -p "$out/vcpkg-$arm/$port"
                  cp "$state/worktrees/ladybird-bench-$arm/Build/vcpkg/buildtrees/$port"/*.log "$out/vcpkg-$arm/$port"/ \
                    2> /dev/null || true
                done || true
            done
            local raw
            raw=$(sed -n 's/.*(raw results: \(.*\))$/\1/p' "$out/bench_pr.log" 2> /dev/null | tail -n 1)
            if [ -n "$raw" ] && [ -d "$raw" ]; then
              cp -R "$raw" "$out/raw-results" || true
            fi
          }
          trap save_logs_and_raw_results EXIT

          src=$state/src
          if [ ! -d "$src/.git" ]; then
            git clone --quiet --filter=blob:none "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" "$src"
          fi
          git -C "$src" fetch --quiet origin master "$HEAD_SHA"
          git -C "$src" checkout --quiet --detach "$HEAD_SHA"

          # Each arm builds with the Rust toolchain its own tree names.
          for sha in $(git -C "$src" merge-base "$HEAD_SHA" origin/master) "$HEAD_SHA"; do
            toolchain_dir=$(mktemp -d)
            git -C "$src" show "${sha}:rust-toolchain.toml" > "$toolchain_dir/rust-toolchain.toml"
            (cd "$toolchain_dir" && rustup toolchain install)
          done

          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench-venv"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench-venv/bin/pip" install --quiet -r web-benchmarks/requirements.txt

          # bench_pr.py won't start on a busy machine, and a job that just finished may still be winding down.
          ncpu=$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN)
          for _ in $(seq 60); do
            if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = macOS ]; then load=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{ print $2 }'); else load=$(cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/loadavg); fi
            awk -v l="$load" -v n="$ncpu" 'BEGIN { exit !(l < n / 4) }' && break
            sleep 10
          done

          args=(--ladybird "$src" --worktree-root "$state/worktrees" --rounds "$ROUNDS" -o "$out/pr-perf-section.md")
          [ "$CALIBRATE" = true ] && args+=(--calibrate)
          [ -n "$BENCHMARKS" ] && args+=(--benchmarks "$BENCHMARKS")
          if [ -n "$FOCUS" ]; then
            read -r -a focus <<< "$FOCUS"
            args+=(--focus "${focus[@]}")
          fi
          status=0
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench-venv/bin/python" web-benchmarks/bench_pr.py "${args[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$out/bench_pr.log" || status=$?

          {
            echo '```'
            grep -E '^(baseline|branch head|A-vs-A|false movers)|BLOCKING|warning:' "$out/bench_pr.log" || true
            echo '```'
            [ -f "$out/pr-perf-section.md" ] && cat "$out/pr-perf-section.md"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "Disk used by the run: $(du -sh "$state" | cut -f1)"
          exit "$status"

      - name: 'Save the calibration'
        if: ${{ inputs.calibrate }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: bench-pr-noise-floor-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: bench-state/cache/ladybird-bench/noise-floor.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 90

      - name: 'Save results as an artifact'
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: bench-pr-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: bench-pr-out/
          retention-days: 90

  report:
    needs: [prepare, bench]
    # A run that a newer run for the same PR cancelled leaves its report to that newer run.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.prepare.result != 'skipped' }}
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404

    # Runs nothing from the PR.
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      # A bench job that lost its runner reports neither success nor failure — so these steps check only that the bench
      # jobs ran, and the description then reports a platform without results as one that didn't finish.
      - name: 'Download the results'
        if: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.pr != '' && needs.bench.result != 'skipped' }}
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: bench-pr-*
          path: results
          merge-multiple: true

      # The section goes between markers at the end of the description, so a later run replaces it in place.
      - name: "Add the results to the PR's description"
        if: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.pr != '' && needs.bench.result != 'skipped' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.pr }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.head }}
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.matrix }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls/${PR}" --jq '.body // ""' > body.md
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, os, re

          claims, details = [], []
          for entry in json.loads(os.environ["MATRIX"])["include"]:
              platform = f"{entry['os_name']} {entry['arch']}"
              path = f"results/{entry['os_name']}-{entry['arch']}/pr-perf-section.md"
              if not os.path.exists(path):
                  claims.append(f"**{platform}:** The run didn't finish; see [its log]({os.environ['RUN_URL']}).")
                  continue
              # bench_pr.py's section: a heading, the claim, then one details block.
              section = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
              claim, _, rest = section.partition("<details>")
              claims.append(f"**{platform}:** " + claim.replace("## Performance", "", 1).strip())
              details.append("<details>" + rest.replace("<summary>Benchmark run details</summary>",
                                                        f"<summary>{platform} run details</summary>", 1).rstrip())

          block = "\n\n".join(["<!-- bench-pr -->", "## Performance", *claims, *details,
                               f"From [a PR benchmarks run]({os.environ['RUN_URL']}) at {os.environ['HEAD_SHA'][:11]}.",
                               "<!-- /bench-pr -->"])
          body = open("body.md", encoding="utf-8").read().replace("\r\n", "\n")
          body = re.sub(r"\s*<!-- bench-pr -->.*?<!-- /bench-pr -->\s*", "\n\n", body, flags=re.S).strip()
          with open("request.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
              json.dump({"body": (body + "\n\n" if body else "") + block + "\n"}, f)
          EOF
          gh api -X PATCH "repos/${REPO}/pulls/${PR}" --input request.json > /dev/null

      - name: 'Remove the benchmark label'
        # A run that a newer run for the same PR cancelled leaves the label to that newer run, which removes it whether
        # the label or a dispatch started it.
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' || needs.prepare.outputs.pr != '') }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || needs.prepare.outputs.pr }}
        run: gh api -X DELETE "repos/${REPO}/issues/${PR}/labels/benchmark" > /dev/null || true

FILE: .github/workflows/build-and-test.yml
name: Build and Test

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      toolchain:
        required: true
        type: string
      os_name:
        required: true
        type: string
      runner_labels:
        required: true
        type: string
      arch:
        required: true
        type: string
      build_preset:
        required: true
        type: string
      clang_plugins:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      container:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'null'
    secrets:
      VCPKG_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID:
        required: false
      VCPKG_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:
        required: false

jobs:
  CI:
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.runner_labels) }}
    container: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.container) }}

    steps:
      # Pull requests can trail behind `master` and can cause breakage if merging before running the CI checks on an updated branch.
      # Luckily, GitHub creates and maintains a merge branch that is updated whenever the target or source branch is modified. By
      # checking this branch out, we gain a stabler `master` at the cost of reproducibility.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge

      - name: Prepare vcpkg source asset staging
        id: vcpkg-assets
        if: >-
          ${{ vars.VCPKG_R2_ENDPOINT != '' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
              && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'schedule') }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          stage_root="$RUNNER_TEMP"
          if [[ "$RUNNER_OS" == Windows ]]; then
            stage_root=$(cygpath -u "$stage_root")
          fi

          stage=$(mktemp -d "$stage_root/vcpkg-assets.XXXXXX")
          if [[ "$RUNNER_OS" == Windows ]]; then
            stage=$(cygpath -m "$stage")
            uri_path="/$stage"
          else
            uri_path="$stage"
          fi

          printf 'path=%s\nurl=file://%s/\n' "$stage" "$uri_path" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build
        uses: $/.github/actions/build
        env:
          VCPKG_ASSET_WRITE_URL: ${{ steps.vcpkg-assets.outputs.url }}
        with:
          os: ${{ inputs.os_name }}
          arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
          toolchain: ${{ inputs.toolchain }}
          build_preset: ${{ inputs.build_preset }}
          clang_plugins: ${{ inputs.clang_plugins }}

      - name: Prepare to publish staged vcpkg source assets
        id: vcpkg-publish
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.vcpkg-assets.outputs.path != '' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          VCPKG_ASSET_STAGE: ${{ steps.vcpkg-assets.outputs.path }}
        run: |
          assets=("$VCPKG_ASSET_STAGE"/*)
          [[ -f "${assets[0]}" ]] || exit 0

          if [[ "$(aws --version 2>/dev/null)" != aws-cli/2.* ]]; then
            aws_version=2.42.3
            installer_dir=$(mktemp -d)

            download_aws_installer() {
              local filename=$1 expected_sha256=$2
              local checksum_command=(sha256sum)
              if [[ "$RUNNER_OS" == macOS ]]; then
                checksum_command=(shasum -a 256)
              fi

              curl -fsSL --retry 3 "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/$filename" -o "$installer_dir/$filename"
              printf '%s  %s\n' "$expected_sha256" "$installer_dir/$filename" | "${checksum_command[@]}" -c -
            }

            case "$RUNNER_OS" in
              Linux)
                arch=$(uname -m)
                case "$arch" in
                  x86_64) sha256=09a4a71458061ce4e6e8c1ddbeb5d128c219ef7c9906b7b92c3b542944c025c8 ;;
                  aarch64) sha256=7c512283f5293c6fb0832ad648198993185889b22ea8b19bcd04c153dabc8643 ;;
                  *) printf 'Unsupported AWS CLI architecture: %s\n' "$arch" >&2; exit 1 ;;
                esac
                installer="awscli-exe-linux-$arch-$aws_version.zip"
                download_aws_installer "$installer" "$sha256"
                unzip -q "$installer_dir/$installer" -d "$installer_dir"
                "$installer_dir/aws/install" --install-dir "$installer_dir/cli" --bin-dir "$installer_dir/bin"
                printf '%s\n' "$installer_dir/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
                ;;
              macOS)
                installer="AWSCLIV2-$aws_version.pkg"
                download_aws_installer "$installer" d98091b3a3d170fa7f9e24c5594a9664aff6dbf048cdd588bfe043e27b3ad239
                sudo installer -pkg "$installer_dir/$installer" -target /
                printf '%s\n' /usr/local/bin >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
                ;;
              Windows)
                installer="AWSCLIV2-$aws_version.msi"
                download_aws_installer "$installer" 68a2d5c5581f72cd9d592ed3005c7bff66613a9854e4d1d303411ccf2fd2b4a1
                MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' msiexec.exe /i "$(cygpath -w "$installer_dir/$installer")" /quiet /norestart
                printf '%s\n' "${PROGRAMFILES:-$ProgramFiles}\\Amazon\\AWSCLIV2" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
                ;;
            esac
          fi

          echo 'ready=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Publish vcpkg source assets to R2
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && steps.vcpkg-publish.outputs.ready == 'true'
              && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
              && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'schedule') }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          VCPKG_ASSET_STAGE: ${{ steps.vcpkg-assets.outputs.path }}
          R2_ENDPOINT: ${{ vars.VCPKG_R2_ENDPOINT }}
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.VCPKG_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.VCPKG_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: auto
        run: |
          : "${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:?Set the VCPKG_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID secret}"
          : "${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:?Set the VCPKG_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY secret}"

          aws --endpoint-url "$R2_ENDPOINT" s3 cp "$VCPKG_ASSET_STAGE/" \
            s3://ladybird-vcpkg-assets/source-assets/ \
            --recursive --only-show-errors \
            --cache-control 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'

      # The macOS AX tests run against this bundle on another machine (see macos-accessibility-tests.yml). So the
      # bundle has to be self-contained. To make it self-contained, this script copies the libraries in, Qt included,
      # adds the Qt platform plugin, re-signs the executables with the entitlements the build used, and tars the result.
      - name: Package the macOS app bundle for the accessibility tests
        if: ${{ inputs.os_name == 'macOS' && inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer' }}
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          "${{ env.pythonLocation }}/bin/python" Meta/package-macos-test-bundle.py \
            --build-dir Build --install-dir Install --output ladybird-app-bundle.tar.gz

      - name: Upload the macOS app bundle
        if: ${{ inputs.os_name == 'macOS' && inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ladybird-app-bundle-${{ inputs.os_name }}-${{ inputs.arch }}-${{ inputs.build_preset }}
          path: ladybird-app-bundle.tar.gz
          compression-level: 0
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: error

      # === TEST ===

      - name: Start PulseAudio
        if: ${{ inputs.os_name == 'Linux' }}
        run: |
          echo "PULSE_SERVER=unix:/tmp/pulse-native" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          pulseaudio --system -D --exit-idle-time=1800 \
            --load="module-native-protocol-unix auth-anonymous=1 socket=/tmp/pulse-native" \
            --load="module-null-sink sink_name=virtual_sink"

      - name: Verify StyleEngine invariants
        if: ${{ inputs.os_name == 'Linux' && (inputs.build_preset == 'Release' || inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer') }}
        timeout-minutes: 5
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build/Tests/LibWeb/test-web
        run: |
          ../../../bin/test-web --verify-style -j10 \
            -f Text/input/css/style-engine/ \
            -f Text/input/css/style-invalidation/

      - name: Check new tests for flakiness
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer' && (inputs.os_name == 'Linux' || inputs.os_name == 'macOS') }}
        timeout-minutes: 30
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags --depth=2 origin "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          "${{ env.pythonLocation }}/bin/python" Meta/check-test-flakiness.py \
            --test-web-binary Build/bin/test-web \
            --base-ref HEAD^1 \
            --deadline-seconds 1200 \
            --python-executable "${{ env.pythonLocation }}/bin/python" \
            | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Cloning WPT normally takes well under a minute, but now and then a clone stalls. Cut a stalled clone off and
      # start over, in a step of its own, so it can't use up the time the smoke tests have.
      - name: Clone WPT
        if: ${{ inputs.os_name == 'Linux' && (inputs.build_preset == 'Release' || inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer') }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            rm -rf Tests/LibWeb/WPT/wpt
            if timeout 180 Meta/WPT.sh update; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "::warning::Cloning WPT failed or stalled (attempt ${attempt} of 3)"
          done
          exit 1

      - name: Run WPT Smoke Tests
        if: ${{ inputs.os_name == 'Linux' && (inputs.build_preset == 'Release' || inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer') }}
        timeout-minutes: 5
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export ASAN_OPTIONS="log_path=\"${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Build/asan.log\""
          export UBSAN_OPTIONS="log_path=\"${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Build/ubsan.log\""
          Meta/WPT.sh run --test-list Tests/LibWeb/WPT/ci-smoke-tests.txt
        env:
          BUILD_LADYBIRD: 'false'
          LADYBIRD_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build/bin/Ladybird
          WEBDRIVER_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build/bin/WebDriver
          WPT_PROCESSES: '4'

      - name: Test
        if: ${{ inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer' }}
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export ASAN_OPTIONS="log_path=\"${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Build/asan.log\""
          export UBSAN_OPTIONS="log_path=\"${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Build/ubsan.log\""
          ctest --preset ${{ inputs.build_preset }} --parallel --output-on-failure -E 'LibWebAccessibilityBridge|AccessibilityBridgeMac' --test-dir Build --timeout 1800

      - name: Test
        if: ${{ inputs.build_preset != 'Fuzzers' && inputs.build_preset != 'All_Debug' && inputs.build_preset != 'Sanitizer' }}
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: ctest --parallel --output-on-failure -E 'LibWebAccessibilityBridge|AccessibilityBridgeMac' --test-dir Build --timeout 1800

      # The AT-SPI2 tests need a Linux build that is neither Sanitizer nor All_Debug:
      # - Sanitizer's ASan-instrumented Qt-on-XCB hits a buffer overflow in libxkbcommon-x11.
      # - All_Debug's ENABLE_ALL_THE_DEBUG_MACROS log volume starves the Qt event loop, so AT-SPI2 registration never
      #   completes within any reasonable wait window.
      # Release builds hit neither problem — so we run these tests on the Release runner.
      - name: Test - LibWeb AT-SPI2 bridge (Release)
        if: ${{ inputs.os_name == 'Linux' && inputs.build_preset == 'Release' }}
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: ctest --output-on-failure --no-tests=error --test-dir Build -R LibWebAccessibilityBridge --timeout 1800

      - name: Upload LibWeb Test Artifacts
        if: ${{ always() && inputs.build_preset != 'Fuzzers' && inputs.build_preset != 'All_Debug' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: libweb-test-artifacts-${{ inputs.os_name }}-${{ inputs.arch }}-${{ inputs.build_preset }}-${{ inputs.toolchain }}-${{ inputs.clang_plugins }}
          path: |
            Build/Tests/LibWeb/test-web/test-dumps/
            Build/**/asan.log.*
            Build/**/ubsan.log.*
          retention-days: 0
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Sanitizer Output
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && inputs.build_preset == 'Sanitizer' }}
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          log_output=$(find Build \( -name 'asan.log.*' -o -name 'ubsan.log.*' \) -exec cat {} \; )
          if [ -z "$log_output" ]; then
            echo "No sanitizer issues found."
          else
            echo "$log_output"
            echo "Sanitizer errors happened while running tests; see the Test step above."
          fi
