META_SOURCE_DIR = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
LADYBIRD_SOURCE_DIR = META_SOURCE_DIR.parent

SEPARATOR = "=" * 80

# Ports that install libraries or headers, yet only run while building.
BUILD_ONLY_PORTS = {"pkgconf"}

# Ports that install neither libraries nor headers, yet end up in what we ship.
DATA_PORTS = {"pdfjs"}

SHIPPED_PORT_DIRECTORIES = {"bin", "Frameworks", "include", "lib"}

LGPL_MARKER = "GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE"

LGPL_LIBRARIES_PATH = pathlib.PurePosixPath("Meta/CMake/lgpl-libraries.txt")

# Release-tools publishes the source archives of the LGPL ports there, for every release that ships them.
THIRD_PARTY_SOURCES_URL = "https://download.ladybird.org/third-party"

# Ladybird's vcpkg asset cache, which holds the source downloads of the ports by their SHA-512.
VCPKG_ASSET_CACHE_URL = "https://vcpkg-assets.ladybird.org/source-assets"

GITHUB_SOURCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^git\+https://github\.com/(?P<repository>[^/@]+/[^/@]+)@(?P<ref>.+)$")
UNSAFE_NAME_CHARACTERS = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._+-]")
GIT_SOURCE_FORMAT = "tar.xz"

CRATE_LICENSE_FILE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(licen[cs]e|copying|copyright|notice|unlicense|patents)", re.IGNORECASE)

C_FAMILY_COMMENT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"/\*.*?\*/|(?:^[ \t]*//[^\n]*\n?)+", re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)
ASSEMBLY_COMMENT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(?:^[ \t]*;[^\n]*\n?)+", re.MULTILINE)
SOURCE_COMMENT_PATTERNS = {
    **dict.fromkeys(["c", "cc", "cpp", "cxx", "h", "hh", "hpp", "hxx", "inc", "m", "mm"], C_FAMILY_COMMENT_PATTERN),
    "asm": ASSEMBLY_COMMENT_PATTERN,
}
LICENSE_NOTICE_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"copyright|public domain|licensed under|permission is hereby granted|spdx-license-identifier", re.IGNORECASE
)


@dataclass
class Port:
    name: str
    version: str
    copyright: str
    spdx_path: pathlib.Path


@dataclass
class FlatpakModule:
    name: str
    version: str
    copyright: str
    definition: dict[str, Any]
    manifest_dir: pathlib.Path


@dataclass
class SourceDownload:
    file_name: str
    sha512: str
    location: str


# What builds a port: the files of its vcpkg port, by their path in it and their SHA-256, and what the port downloads.
# vcpkg records both in the SPDX document that it installs with the port.
@dataclass
class PortSource:
    port: Port
    port_files: dict[str, str]
    downloads: list[SourceDownload]

    # The name says what the archive holds, so that every build that uses the same source names the same archive.
    def archive_name(self) -> str:
        lines = [f"port {path} {digest}" for path, digest in sorted(self.port_files.items())]
        lines += sorted(f"download {download.file_name} {download.sha512}" for download in self.downloads)
        digest = hashlib.sha256("\n".join(lines).encode()).hexdigest()
        version = self.port.version.partition("#")[0]
        return UNSAFE_NAME_CHARACTERS.sub("_", f"{self.port.name}-{version}-{digest[:12]}") + ".tar"


@dataclass
class CrateLicense:
    text: str
    crates: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def read_text(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").replace("\r\n", "\n").strip("\n")


def parse_control_paragraphs(path: pathlib.Path) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    paragraphs = []
    for block in read_text(path).split("\n\n"):
        paragraph = dict(re.findall(r"^([\w-]+): (.*)$", block, re.MULTILINE))
        if paragraph:
            paragraphs.append(paragraph)
    return paragraphs


# NOTE: Whole source files get cut down to their license notices here.
#
# A port's copyright file is whatever its portfile hands to vcpkg_install_copyright(), which joins the files it is given
# under a "<file name>:" heading each. Some ports hand it an entire source file, since the only copy of a notice is in
# a comment of that file: libspng passes spng.c, sdl3 passes stb_image.h and dav1d passes x86inc.asm, which is over
# half a megabyte of code between the three of them.
#
# So of every part whose heading names a C, C++, Objective-C or NASM file, only the comments that carry a copyright or
# license notice are kept, and "(license notices only)" is added to its heading. Everything else is copied as it is:
# parts under any other heading, copyright files without headings, and a source file in which no such comment is found.
# The headings are told apart from the text by their looks alone: a line of its own between blank lines, ending in a
# colon, without spaces, and with a dot or a capital in it, which rules out the labels of C. A line in a source file
# that still looks like one ends the part early, which leaves the rest of that file in place.
def trim_source_files(copyright_text: str) -> str:
    lines = copyright_text.split("\n")

    def is_heading(index: int) -> bool:
        line = lines[index]
        if not line.endswith(":") or " " in line or "/" in line:
            return False
        if "." not in line and line == line.lower():
            return False
        if index > 0 and lines[index - 1] != "":
            return False
        return index + 1 < len(lines) and lines[index + 1] == ""

    headings = [index for index in range(len(lines)) if is_heading(index)]
    if not headings:
        return copyright_text

    parts = []
    if preamble := "\n".join(lines[: headings[0]]).strip("\n"):
        parts.append(preamble)
    for heading, next_heading in zip(headings, headings[1:] + [len(lines)]):
        name = lines[heading][:-1]
        body = "\n".join(lines[heading + 1 : next_heading]).strip("\n")

        if comment_pattern := SOURCE_COMMENT_PATTERNS.get(name.rpartition(".")[2]):
            comments = [match.group(0).strip("\n") for match in comment_pattern.finditer(body)]
            notices = [comment for comment in comments if LICENSE_NOTICE_PATTERN.search(comment)]
            if notices:
                name = f"{name} (license notices only)"
                body = "\n\n".join(notices)

        parts.append(f"{name}:\n\n{body}")

    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def port_is_shipped(name: str, installed_files: list[str], triplet: str) -> bool:
    if name in BUILD_ONLY_PORTS:
        return False
    if name in DATA_PORTS:
        return True

    for installed_file in installed_files:
        parts = pathlib.PurePosixPath(installed_file).parts
        if len(parts) > 2 and parts[0] == triplet and parts[1] in SHIPPED_PORT_DIRECTORIES:
            return True
    return False


def read_lgpl_libraries(source_dir: pathlib.Path) -> set[str]:
    lines = read_text(source_dir / LGPL_LIBRARIES_PATH).splitlines()
    return {line.strip() for line in lines if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#")}


def collect_vcpkg_ports(installed_dir: pathlib.Path, triplet: str) -> list[Port]:
    ports = []

    for paragraph in parse_control_paragraphs(installed_dir / "vcpkg" / "status"):
        if "Feature" in paragraph or paragraph.get("Architecture") != triplet:
            continue
        if paragraph.get("Status") != "install ok installed":
            continue

        name = paragraph["Package"]
        version = paragraph["Version"]
        if port_version := paragraph.get("Port-Version"):
            version = f"{version}#{port_version}"

        list_files = list((installed_dir / "vcpkg" / "info").glob(f"{name}_*_{triplet}.list"))
        if len(list_files) != 1:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Expected one file list for the vcpkg port {name}, found {len(list_files)}")
        if not port_is_shipped(name, read_text(list_files[0]).splitlines(), triplet):
            continue

        copyright_file = installed_dir / triplet / "share" / name / "copyright"
        if not copyright_file.is_file():
            raise RuntimeError(f"The vcpkg port {name} installs files we ship, but no copyright file")

        spdx_path = installed_dir / triplet / "share" / name / "vcpkg.spdx.json"
        ports.append(Port(name, version, trim_source_files(read_text(copyright_file)), spdx_path))

    return sorted(ports, key=lambda port: port.name.lower())


def read_port_source(port: Port) -> PortSource:
    try:
        spdx = json.loads(port.spdx_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        raise RuntimeError(f"The vcpkg port {port.name} has no readable SPDX document: {error}") from error

    files = {entry["SPDXID"]: entry for entry in spdx.get("files", [])}
    port_files = {}
    for relationship in spdx.get("relationships", []):
        if relationship["spdxElementId"] != "SPDXRef-port" or relationship["relationshipType"] != "CONTAINS":
            continue
        entry = files[relationship["relatedSpdxElement"]]
        digests = {checksum["algorithm"]: checksum["checksumValue"] for checksum in entry.get("checksums", [])}
        path = pathlib.PurePosixPath(entry["fileName"])
        if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts or "SHA256" not in digests:
            raise RuntimeError(f"The SPDX document of {port.name} lists the port file {entry['fileName']}")
        port_files[path.as_posix()] = digests["SHA256"].lower()
    if not port_files:
        raise RuntimeError(f"The SPDX document of {port.name} lists no files of its port")

    downloads = []
    for package in spdx.get("packages", []):
        if not package["SPDXID"].startswith("SPDXRef-resource-"):
            continue
        digests = {checksum["algorithm"]: checksum["checksumValue"] for checksum in package.get("checksums", [])}
        location = package.get("downloadLocation", "")
        if "SHA512" not in digests:
            raise RuntimeError(f"The SPDX document of {port.name} gives no SHA-512 of {location}")
        if github := GITHUB_SOURCE_PATTERN.match(location):
            # The file name that vcpkg_from_github() gives the archive that it downloads.
            file_name = f"{github['repository'].replace('/', '-')}-{github['ref'].replace('/', '_-')}.tar.gz"
        else:
            file_name = package.get("name") or urllib.parse.urlparse(location).path.rpartition("/")[2]
        if not file_name or UNSAFE_NAME_CHARACTERS.search(file_name) or file_name.startswith("."):
            raise RuntimeError(f"The SPDX document of {port.name} names the download {location} as {file_name!r}")
        sha512 = digests["SHA512"].lower()
        if same_name := next((download for download in downloads if download.file_name == file_name), None):
            if same_name.sha512 != sha512:
                raise RuntimeError(f"The SPDX document of {port.name} names two different downloads {file_name}")
            continue
        downloads.append(SourceDownload(file_name, sha512, location))

    return PortSource(port, port_files, downloads)


def configured_overlay_ports(source_dir: pathlib.Path) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    configuration = json.loads(read_text(source_dir / "vcpkg-configuration.json"))
    return [source_dir / path for path in configuration.get("overlay-ports", [])]


def read_directory_files(directory: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    return {
        path.relative_to(directory).as_posix(): path.read_bytes()
        for path in sorted(directory.rglob("*"))
        if path.is_file()
    }


def read_git_tree(repository: pathlib.Path, tree: str) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    archive = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repository), "archive", "--format=tar", tree], check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE
    ).stdout
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(archive)) as tar:
        return {
            member.name: file.read()
            for member in tar.getmembers()
            if member.isfile() and (file := tar.extractfile(member))
        }


def versioned_port_trees(vcpkg_root: pathlib.Path, source: PortSource) -> list[str]:
    name = source.port.name
    versions_file = vcpkg_root / "versions" / f"{name[0]}-" / f"{name}.json"
    if not versions_file.is_file():
        return []
    version, _, port_version = source.port.version.partition("#")
    trees = []
    for entry in json.loads(read_text(versions_file))["versions"]:
        names = [entry.get(key) for key in ("version", "version-semver", "version-date", "version-string")]
        if version in names and str(entry.get("port-version", 0)) == (port_version or "0"):
            trees.append(entry["git-tree"])
    return trees


# vcpkg takes an overlay port before the port of its registry, and the port of a version that vcpkg.json pins from
# the history of the registry. Of these, the one whose files are those that the SPDX document lists is the one that
# built the port.
def read_port_files(source_dir: pathlib.Path, vcpkg_root: pathlib.Path, source: PortSource) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    name = source.port.name
    candidates = [
        functools.partial(read_directory_files, overlay / name)
        for overlay in configured_overlay_ports(source_dir)
        if (overlay / name / "vcpkg.json").is_file()
    ]
    candidates += [
        functools.partial(read_git_tree, vcpkg_root, tree) for tree in versioned_port_trees(vcpkg_root, source)
    ]
    if (vcpkg_root / "ports" / name / "vcpkg.json").is_file():
        candidates.append(functools.partial(read_directory_files, vcpkg_root / "ports" / name))

    for candidate in candidates:
        files = candidate()
        digests = {path: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() for path, data in files.items()}
        if digests == source.port_files:
            return files
    raise RuntimeError(f"Found no port of {name} {source.port.version} with the files that its SPDX document lists")


def download_source(download: SourceDownload, downloads_dir: Optional[pathlib.Path], destination: pathlib.Path) -> None:
    def matches(path: pathlib.Path) -> bool:
        digest = hashlib.sha512()
        with open(path, "rb") as file:
            while chunk := file.read(1 << 20):
                digest.update(chunk)
        return digest.hexdigest() == download.sha512

    if downloads_dir and (downloads_dir / download.file_name).is_file() and matches(downloads_dir / download.file_name):
        shutil.copyfile(downloads_dir / download.file_name, destination)
        return

    urls = [f"{VCPKG_ASSET_CACHE_URL}/{download.sha512}"]
    if github := GITHUB_SOURCE_PATTERN.match(download.location):
        urls.append(f"https://github.com/{github['repository']}/archive/{github['ref']}.tar.gz")
    elif download.location.startswith("https://"):
        urls.append(download.location)

    failures = []
    for url in urls:
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response, open(destination, "wb") as file:
                shutil.copyfileobj(response, file)
        except (OSError, urllib.error.URLError) as error:
            failures.append(f"{url}: {error}")
            continue
        if matches(destination):
            return
        failures.append(f"{url}: another SHA-512")
    raise RuntimeError(f"Could not download {download.file_name}:\n  " + "\n  ".join(failures))


# The archive holds nothing that differs between the machines that make it, so that every build of the same source
# makes the very same archive.
def add_to_archive(archive: tarfile.TarFile, name: str, data: bytes) -> None:
    info = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
    info.size = len(data)
    info.mode = 0o644
    info.mtime = 0
    archive.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))


def write_port_archive(
    source: PortSource, port_files: dict[str, bytes], work_dir: pathlib.Path, destination: pathlib.Path
) -> None:
    root = source.archive_name().removesuffix(".tar")
    readme = "\n".join(
        [
            f"The source code of {source.port.name} {source.port.version}, as Ladybird builds it with vcpkg.",
            "",
            "port/ holds the vcpkg port of the library: its build scripts and our patches. The other files are the",
            "source archives that the port downloads, unchanged:",
            "",
            *[f"  {download.file_name}: {download.location}" for download in source.downloads],
            "",
        ]
    )
    with tarfile.open(destination, "w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT) as archive:
        add_to_archive(archive, f"{root}/README", readme.encode())
        for path, data in sorted(port_files.items()):
            add_to_archive(archive, f"{root}/port/{path}", data)
        for download in sorted(source.downloads, key=lambda download: download.file_name):
            add_to_archive(archive, f"{root}/{download.file_name}", (work_dir / download.file_name).read_bytes())


def package_third_party_sources(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    if not args.vcpkg_installed_dir or not args.vcpkg_triplet or not args.vcpkg_root:
        raise RuntimeError("Packaging the sources of the LGPL ports needs the vcpkg root, installed tree and triplet")

    ports = collect_vcpkg_ports(args.vcpkg_installed_dir, args.vcpkg_triplet)
    sources = [read_port_source(port) for port in ports if LGPL_MARKER in port.copyright]
    downloads_dir = args.vcpkg_root / "downloads"

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work:
        work_dir = pathlib.Path(work)
        archives = []
        for source in sources:
            port_files = read_port_files(args.source_dir, args.vcpkg_root, source)
            source_dir = work_dir / source.port.name
            source_dir.mkdir()
            for download in source.downloads:
                download_source(
                    download, downloads_dir if downloads_dir.is_dir() else None, source_dir / download.file_name
                )
            write_port_archive(source, port_files, source_dir, work_dir / source.archive_name())
            archives.append(work_dir / source.archive_name())
            print(f"Packaged the source of {source.port.name} {source.port.version} as {source.archive_name()}")

        write_bundle(args.third_party_sources, archives)


def write_bundle(path: pathlib.Path, archives: list[pathlib.Path]) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tarfile.open(path, "w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT) as bundle:
        for archive in archives:
            bundle.add(archive, arcname=archive.name)


def flatpak_lgpl_modules(manifest_path: pathlib.Path, source_dir: pathlib.Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    lgpl_libraries = read_lgpl_libraries(source_dir)
    found = []
    pending = list(json.loads(read_text(manifest_path))["modules"])
    while pending:
        module = pending.pop(0)
        if isinstance(module, str):
            raise RuntimeError(f"The Flatpak manifest includes the module file {module}, which this script cannot read")
        pending += module.get("modules", [])
        if module["name"] in lgpl_libraries:
            found.append(module)
    return found


def flatpak_patch(module: dict[str, Any], source: dict[str, Any], manifest_dir: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    if "path" not in source:
        raise RuntimeError(f"A patch of the Flatpak module {module['name']} has no single path")
    return manifest_dir / source["path"]


# Like the archive of a vcpkg port, the name says what the archive holds: the module that builds the library, which
# pins the commits and digests of its sources, the format that its git sources are packed in, and the patches that it
# applies.
def flatpak_archive_name(module: dict[str, Any], manifest_dir: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    lines = [f"module {json.dumps(module, sort_keys=True)}"]
    for source in module["sources"]:
        if source.get("type") == "git":
            lines.append(f"git {GIT_SOURCE_FORMAT}")
        if source.get("type") == "patch":
            path = flatpak_patch(module, source, manifest_dir)
            lines.append(f"patch {source['path']} {hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}")
    digest = hashlib.sha256("\n".join(lines).encode()).hexdigest()
    version = flatpak_module_version(module) or "source"
    return UNSAFE_NAME_CHARACTERS.sub("_", f"{module['name']}-{version}-{digest[:12]}") + ".tar"


def flatpak_module_version(module: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    for source in module.get("sources", []):
        if isinstance(source, dict) and source.get("type") == "git":
            return source.get("tag") or source.get("commit", "")[:12]
        if isinstance(source, dict) and source.get("type") == "archive":
            name = urllib.parse.urlparse(source["url"]).path.rpartition("/")[2]
            version = re.sub(r"\.tar(\.[a-z0-9]+)?$|\.zip$", "", name).removeprefix(f"{module['name']}-")
            return version[:12] if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", version) else version
    return ""


# flatpak-builder 1.4.5 and newer record the license files of every module that they build in a directory of the
# module's name. A release needs them, while other builds may use an older flatpak-builder. A module that cleans up all
# of its files, such as a build tool, ships nothing.
def collect_flatpak_modules(
    manifest_path: pathlib.Path, licenses_dir: pathlib.Path, release: bool
) -> list[FlatpakModule]:
    manifest_dir = manifest_path.resolve().parent
    modules = []
    pending = list(json.loads(read_text(manifest_path))["modules"])
    while pending:
        module = pending.pop(0)
        if isinstance(module, str):
            raise RuntimeError(f"The Flatpak manifest includes the module file {module}, which this script cannot read")
        pending += module.get("modules", [])
        if module["name"] == "Ladybird" or module.get("cleanup") == ["*"]:
            continue
        directory = licenses_dir / module["name"]
        files = sorted(path for path in directory.iterdir() if path.is_file()) if directory.is_dir() else []
        if not files:
            message = (
                f"The Flatpak module {module['name']} ships files, but has no license files in {directory}, where "
                "flatpak-builder 1.4.5 and newer record them"
            )
            if release:
                raise RuntimeError(message)
            print(f"warning: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
        modules.append(
            FlatpakModule(
                module["name"],
                flatpak_module_version(module),
                "\n\n".join(read_text(path).strip() for path in files) + "\n"
                if files
                else "flatpak-builder recorded no license files of this module.\n",
                module,
                manifest_dir,
            )
        )
    return sorted(modules, key=lambda module: module.name.lower())


def fetch_git_source(source: dict[str, Any], work_dir: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
    reference = source.get("commit") or f"refs/tags/{source['tag']}"
    repository = work_dir / "git"
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "--quiet", "--bare", str(repository)], check=True)
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repository), "fetch", "--quiet", "--depth=1", source["url"], reference], check=True
    )
    commit = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repository), "rev-parse", "FETCH_HEAD^{commit}"],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    ).stdout.strip()
    if source.get("commit") and commit != source["commit"]:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{source['url']} has {commit} at {reference}, not {source['commit']}")
    name = source["url"].rstrip("/").removesuffix(".git").rpartition("/")[2]
    root = f"{name}-{source.get('tag') or commit}"
    archive = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repository), "archive", "--format=tar", f"--prefix={root}/", commit],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    ).stdout
    shutil.rmtree(repository)
    return f"{root}.{GIT_SOURCE_FORMAT}", lzma.compress(archive, preset=9 | lzma.PRESET_EXTREME)


def fetch_archive_source(source: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(source["url"], timeout=60) as response:
        data = response.read()
    if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != source.get("sha256"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{source['url']} does not have the SHA-256 that the Flatpak manifest names")
    return source.get("dest-filename") or urllib.parse.urlparse(source["url"]).path.rpartition("/")[2], data


def write_flatpak_module_archive(
    module: dict[str, Any], manifest_dir: pathlib.Path, work_dir: pathlib.Path, destination: pathlib.Path
) -> None:
    files: dict[str, bytes] = {}
    listing = []
    for source in module["sources"]:
        kind = source.get("type")
        if kind == "git":
            name, data = fetch_git_source(source, work_dir)
            listing.append(f"  {name}: the tree of {source['url']} at {source.get('tag') or source['commit']}")
        elif kind == "archive":
            name, data = fetch_archive_source(source)
            listing.append(f"  {name}: {source['url']}")
        elif kind == "patch":
            path = flatpak_patch(module, source, manifest_dir)
            name, data = f"patches/{path.name}", path.read_bytes()
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"The Flatpak module {module['name']} has a {kind} source, which this script cannot read"
            )
        if name in files or UNSAFE_NAME_CHARACTERS.search(name.removeprefix("patches/")):
            raise RuntimeError(f"The Flatpak module {module['name']} names the source {name!r} unsafely or twice")
        files[name] = data

    root = destination.name.removesuffix(".tar")
    readme = "\n".join(
        [
            f"The source code of {module['name']}, as the Ladybird Flatpak builds it with flatpak-builder.",
            "",
            "flatpak-module.json is the module of the Flatpak manifest that builds the library, and patches/ holds",
            "our patches, which it applies in order. The other files are the sources that it fetches:",
            "",
            *listing,
            "",
        ]
    )
    with tarfile.open(destination, "w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT) as archive:
        add_to_archive(archive, f"{root}/README", readme.encode())
        add_to_archive(archive, f"{root}/flatpak-module.json", (json.dumps(module, indent=4) + "\n").encode())
        for name, data in sorted(files.items()):
            add_to_archive(archive, f"{root}/{name}", data)


def package_flatpak_third_party_sources(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    manifest_dir = args.flatpak_manifest.resolve().parent
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work:
        work_dir = pathlib.Path(work)
        archives = []
        for module in flatpak_lgpl_modules(args.flatpak_manifest, args.source_dir):
            name = flatpak_archive_name(module, manifest_dir)
            write_flatpak_module_archive(module, manifest_dir, work_dir, work_dir / name)
            archives.append(work_dir / name)
            print(f"Packaged the source of {module['name']} as {name}")
        write_bundle(args.third_party_sources, archives)


def cargo_metadata(cargo: str, source_dir: pathlib.Path, rust_target: Optional[str], offline: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
    command = [cargo, "metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--locked", "--all-features"]
    if rust_target:
        command += ["--filter-platform", rust_target]
    if offline:
        command.append("--offline")

    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=source_dir, check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    return json.loads(result.stdout)


def linked_third_party_crates(metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    packages = {package["id"]: package for package in metadata["packages"]}
    nodes = {node["id"]: node for node in metadata["resolve"]["nodes"]}

    visited = set()
    pending = list(metadata["workspace_members"])
    while pending:
        package_id = pending.pop()
        if package_id in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(package_id)

        for dependency in nodes[package_id]["deps"]:
            if any(dep_kind["kind"] is None for dep_kind in dependency["dep_kinds"]):
                pending.append(dependency["pkg"])

    crates = [packages[package_id] for package_id in visited if packages[package_id]["source"] is not None]
    return sorted(crates, key=lambda crate: (crate["name"].lower(), crate["version"]))


def crate_license_files(crate: dict[str, Any]) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    crate_dir = pathlib.Path(crate["manifest_path"]).parent

    license_files = []
    for entry in sorted(crate_dir.iterdir(), key=lambda entry: entry.name.lower()):
        if not CRATE_LICENSE_FILE_PATTERN.match(entry.name):
            continue
        if entry.is_dir():
            license_files += sorted(path for path in entry.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
        else:
            license_files.append(entry)

    if declared_file := crate.get("license_file"):
        declared_path = (crate_dir / declared_file).resolve()
        if declared_path.is_file() and declared_path not in [path.resolve() for path in license_files]:
            license_files.append(declared_path)

    return license_files


def describe_crate_without_license_file(crate: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    lines = [
        "This crate does not ship a license file.",
        f"License: {crate['license']}",
    ]
    if authors := crate.get("authors"):
        lines.append(f"Authors: {', '.join(authors)}")
    if repository := crate.get("repository") or crate.get("homepage"):
        lines.append(f"Source: {repository}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def collect_crate_licenses(crates: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[CrateLicense]:
    licenses_by_digest: dict[str, CrateLicense] = {}

    def add(crate: dict[str, Any], text: str) -> None:
        normalized = "\n".join(line.rstrip() for line in text.splitlines()).strip()
        digest = hashlib.sha256(normalized.encode()).hexdigest()
        crate_license = licenses_by_digest.setdefault(digest, CrateLicense(normalized))

        label = f"{crate['name']} {crate['version']}"
        if label not in crate_license.crates:
            crate_license.crates.append(label)

    for crate in crates:
        if crate.get("license") is None and crate.get("license_file") is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"The crate {crate['name']} {crate['version']} declares no license")

        license_files = crate_license_files(crate)
        if not license_files:
            add(crate, describe_crate_without_license_file(crate))
        for license_file in license_files:
            add(crate, read_text(license_file))

    return sorted(licenses_by_digest.values(), key=lambda crate_license: crate_license.crates[0].lower())


def section(title: str, body: str) -> str:
    return f"{SEPARATOR}\n{title}\n{SEPARATOR}\n\n{body}\n"


def generate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    ports = []
    if args.vcpkg_installed_dir and args.vcpkg_triplet:
        ports = collect_vcpkg_ports(args.vcpkg_installed_dir, args.vcpkg_triplet)

    metadata = cargo_metadata(args.cargo, args.source_dir, args.rust_target, args.offline)
    crates = linked_third_party_crates(metadata)
    crate_licenses = collect_crate_licenses(crates)

    modules = []
    if args.flatpak_manifest:
        if not args.flatpak_licenses_dir:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "The licenses of a Flatpak build need the directory that flatpak-builder records them in"
            )
        modules = collect_flatpak_modules(args.flatpak_manifest, args.flatpak_licenses_dir, args.release)

    lgpl_ports = [port for port in ports if LGPL_MARKER in port.copyright]

    lgpl_libraries = read_lgpl_libraries(args.source_dir)
    unlisted = [port.name for port in lgpl_ports if port.name not in lgpl_libraries]
    unlisted += [
        module.name for module in modules if LGPL_MARKER in module.copyright and module.name not in lgpl_libraries
    ]
    if unlisted:
        raise RuntimeError(f"LGPL libraries missing from {LGPL_LIBRARIES_PATH}: {', '.join(unlisted)}")

    # Each with the archive that release-tools publishes its source code in.
    lgpl = [
        (f"{port.name} {port.version}", lambda port=port: read_port_source(port).archive_name()) for port in lgpl_ports
    ]
    lgpl += [
        (
            f"{module.name} {module.version}",
            lambda module=module: flatpak_archive_name(module.definition, module.manifest_dir),
        )
        for module in modules
        if module.name in lgpl_libraries
    ]

    introduction = [
        "Ladybird is distributed under the BSD 2-Clause License below. It includes the third-party software listed",
        "after that, under the licenses reproduced with each of them.",
    ]
    if lgpl and args.release:
        introduction += [
            "",
            "This release of Ladybird uses the following libraries under the GNU Lesser General Public License. The",
            "source code of each, with our patches and build scripts, is at the address below it:",
            "",
        ]
        for library, archive_name in lgpl:
            introduction += [f"  {library}", f"    {THIRD_PARTY_SOURCES_URL}/{archive_name()}"]
        introduction += [
            "",
            "The source code of Ladybird at https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird contains everything needed to",
            "build it against modified versions of these libraries.",
        ]
    elif lgpl:
        introduction += [
            "",
            "This build of Ladybird uses the following libraries under the GNU Lesser General Public License:",
            "",
            *[f"  {library}" for library, _ in lgpl],
            "",
            "The source code of Ladybird at https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird contains everything needed to",
            "build it against modified versions of these libraries, and the build downloads the source code of each",
            "of them in the version listed here.",
        ]

    output = ["\n".join(introduction) + "\n"]
    output.append(section("Ladybird", read_text(args.source_dir / "LICENSE")))

    for port in ports:
        output.append(section(f"{port.name} {port.version}", port.copyright))

    for module in modules:
        output.append(section(f"{module.name} {module.version}".strip(), module.copyright))

    for crate_license in crate_licenses:
        title = "\n".join(f"{crate} (Rust crate)" for crate in crate_license.crates)
        output.append(section(title, crate_license.text))

    return "\n".join(output)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Collects the licenses of Ladybird and of the third-party software a build of it includes"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--output", "-o", type=pathlib.Path)
    parser.add_argument("--source-dir", type=pathlib.Path, default=LADYBIRD_SOURCE_DIR)
    parser.add_argument("--vcpkg-installed-dir", type=pathlib.Path)
    parser.add_argument("--vcpkg-triplet")
    parser.add_argument("--cargo", default="cargo")
    parser.add_argument("--rust-target")
    parser.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--release", action="store_true", help="name where release-tools publishes the source of each LGPL port"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--third-party-sources",
        type=pathlib.Path,
        help="instead of the licenses, write an archive with the source archive of each LGPL port to this path",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--vcpkg-root", type=pathlib.Path, default=os.environ.get("VCPKG_ROOT"))
    parser.add_argument(
        "--flatpak-manifest",
        type=pathlib.Path,
        help="list the modules of this Flatpak manifest, or with --third-party-sources, package its LGPL modules",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--flatpak-licenses-dir", type=pathlib.Path, help="where flatpak-builder records the license files of modules"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.third_party_sources:
        try:
            if args.flatpak_manifest:
                package_flatpak_third_party_sources(args)
            else:
                package_third_party_sources(args)
        except (RuntimeError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
            print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        return 0

    if not args.output:
        parser.error("the following arguments are required: --output/-o")

    try:
        contents = generate(args)
    except (RuntimeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_bytes(contents.encode("utf-8"))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FILE: Meta/generate-style-load-page.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a local page for style-arrival measurements.

A real page load is network-dominated and cannot see a per-element style regression. This one can:
it is one document, no network, and its cost is almost entirely deciding what matches what.

The seed is fixed so two builds see the same document, and every knob is separate so a measurement
can vary exactly one property of the page - which is the method that found what profiling did not.

    ./Meta/generate-style-load-page.py > /tmp/style-load.html
    ./Meta/generate-style-load-page.py --rules 200 --shapes '.c' > /tmp/one-shape.html

Then, from the build directory:

    ./bin/Ladybird.app/Contents/MacOS/WebDriver --headless -p 4540 &
    ./Meta/measure-style-load.py 4540 file:///tmp/style-load.html
"""

import argparse
import random

# The mix a page of hand-written CSS has, in rough proportion. `--shapes` replaces it wholesale so
# one shape can be measured on its own.
DEFAULT_SHAPES = [
    ".c{i}",
    ".c{i}",
    "div.c{i}",
    ".c{i} .d{i}",
    ".c{i} > .d{i}",
    '[data-k="{i}"]',
    ".c{i}:hover, .d{i}:first-child",
]

DECLARATIONS = [
    "color: rgb({r}, {g}, {b})",
    "border-top-width: {i}px",
    "margin-left: {i}px",
    "letter-spacing: {i}px",
]


def rules(count, shapes, rng):
    for i in range(count):
        shape = shapes[i % len(shapes)]
        declaration = DECLARATIONS[i % len(DECLARATIONS)]
        yield "%s { %s }" % (
            shape.format(i=i),
            declaration.format(i=i % 20, r=rng.randrange(256), g=rng.randrange(256), b=rng.randrange(256)),
        )


def elements(count, pool, depth, rng):
    open_tags = []
    for i in range(count):
        # A tree rather than a list, so descendant and child combinators have something to walk.
        if len(open_tags) >= depth or (open_tags and rng.random() < 0.35):
            yield "</%s>" % open_tags.pop()
        tag = "div" if i % 3 else "span"
        classes = "c%d d%d" % (rng.randrange(pool), rng.randrange(pool))
        yield '<%s class="%s" data-k="%d">' % (tag, classes, rng.randrange(pool))
        open_tags.append(tag)
    while open_tags:
        yield "</%s>" % open_tags.pop()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--elements", type=int, default=20000)
    parser.add_argument("--rules", type=int, default=1200)
    parser.add_argument("--depth", type=int, default=12)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260727)
    parser.add_argument("--shapes", help="comma-separated selector templates, `{i}` for the rule index")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--unshared",
        action="store_true",
        help="give every element a class of its own, declaring a value nothing else declares, so "
        "that style sharing cannot answer for any of them. This is the page that measures what one "
        "computed style costs: on a page whose elements share, four in five are answered from "
        "another element and the cost of building one is invisible.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--name-pool",
        type=int,
        help="how many distinct class and attribute names the elements draw from, when that has to "
        "stay fixed while the rule count varies (defaults to the rule count)",
    )
    arguments = parser.parse_args()

    shapes = arguments.shapes.split(",") if arguments.shapes else DEFAULT_SHAPES
    rng = random.Random(arguments.seed)

    print("<!DOCTYPE html>")
    print("<meta charset=utf-8>")
    print("<title>style load</title>")
    print("<style>")
    for rule in rules(arguments.rules, shapes, rng):
        print(rule)
    if arguments.unshared:
        for index in range(arguments.elements):
            print(
                ".u%d { color: rgb(%d, %d, %d); margin-left: %dpx }"
                % (index, index % 256, (index * 7) % 256, (index * 13) % 256, index % 40)
            )
    print("</style>")
    pool = arguments.name_pool or arguments.rules
    unique = 0
    for element in elements(arguments.elements, pool, arguments.depth, rng):
        if arguments.unshared and element.startswith("<") and not element.startswith("</"):
            element = element.replace('class="', 'class="u%d ' % unique, 1)
            unique += 1
        print(element, end="")
    print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

FILE: Meta/Generators/embed_as_string.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
r"""
Embeds a file into a String, a la #embed from C++23
"""

import argparse
import sys


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(epilog=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("input", help="input file to stringify")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True, help="output file")
    parser.add_argument("-n", "--variable-name", required=True, help="name of the C++ variable")
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--namespace", required=False, help="C++ namespace to put the string into")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("#include <AK/String.h>\n")
        if args.namespace:
            f.write(f"namespace {args.namespace} {{\n")
        f.write(f"extern String const& {args.variable_name};\n")
        f.write(f'String const& {args.variable_name} = *new String(R"~~~(')
        with open(args.input, "r", encoding="utf-8") as input:
            for line in input.readlines():
                f.write(f"{line}")
        f.write(')~~~"_string);\n')
        if args.namespace:
            f.write("}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FILE: Meta/Generators/generate_dom_tree.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import re

from html.parser import HTMLParser
from typing import Dict
from typing import List
from typing import Optional
from typing import Set
from typing import Tuple

# HTML void elements that cannot have children
HTML_VOID_ELEMENTS = frozenset(
    [
        "area",
        "base",
        "br",
        "col",
        "embed",
        "hr",
        "img",
        "input",
        "link",
        "meta",
        "param",
        "source",
        "track",
        "wbr",
    ]
)


def parse_html_tag_header(path: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
    result: Dict[str, str] = {}
    pattern = re.compile(r'__ENUMERATE_HTML_TAG\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\)')
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            m = pattern.search(line)
            if m:
                result[m.group(2)] = m.group(1)
    return result


def parse_html_attribute_header(path: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
    result: Dict[str, str] = {}
    pattern = re.compile(r'__ENUMERATE_HTML_ATTRIBUTE\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\)')
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            m = pattern.search(line)
            if m:
                result[m.group(2)] = m.group(1)
    return result


def parse_svg_tag_header(path: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
    result: Dict[str, str] = {}
    pattern = re.compile(r'__ENUMERATE_SVG_TAG\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\)')
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            m = pattern.search(line)
            if m:
                result[m.group(2).lower()] = m.group(1)
    return result


def parse_svg_attribute_header(path: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
    result: Dict[str, str] = {}
    pattern = re.compile(r'__ENUMERATE_SVG_ATTRIBUTE\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\)')
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            m = pattern.search(line)
            if m:
                result[m.group(2).lower()] = m.group(1)
    return result


non_identifier_character_regex = re.compile(r"\W+")


def to_snake_case(string: str) -> str:
    return non_identifier_character_regex.sub("_", string)


def to_pascal_case(string: str) -> str:
    return non_identifier_character_regex.sub(" ", string).title().replace(" ", "")


def resolve_tag(tag_name: str, in_svg: bool, html_tags: Dict[str, str], svg_tags: Dict[str, str]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    if in_svg and tag_name in svg_tags:
        return "Namespace::SVG", f"SVG::TagNames::{svg_tags[tag_name]}"

    assert tag_name in html_tags
    return "Namespace::HTML", f"HTML::TagNames::{html_tags[tag_name]}"


def resolve_attribute(
    attribute_name: str, in_svg: bool, html_attributes: Dict[str, str], svg_attributes: Dict[str, str]
) -> str:
    if in_svg and attribute_name in svg_attributes:
        return f"SVG::AttributeNames::{svg_attributes[attribute_name]}"

    assert attribute_name in html_attributes
    return f"HTML::AttributeNames::{html_attributes[attribute_name]}"


def bits_for_count(count: int) -> int:
    bits = 8
    while bits < 64:
        if count < 2 ^ bits:
            return bits
        bits <<= 1
    return bits


class DOMElement:
    def __init__(self, var_name: str, tag: str, option: Optional[str]):
        self.var_name = var_name
        self.tag = tag
        self.option = option


class DOMTreeParser(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(
        self,
        struct_name: str,
        html_tags: Dict[str, str],
        html_attributes: Dict[str, str],
        svg_tags: Dict[str, str],
        svg_attributes: Dict[str, str],
        input_dir: str,
    ):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=False)
        self.struct_name = struct_name
        self.html_tags = html_tags
        self.html_attributes = html_attributes
        self.svg_tags = svg_tags
        self.svg_attributes = svg_attributes
        self.input_dir = input_dir

        self.lines: List[str] = []
        self.named_fields: List[str] = []
        self.unnamed_element_counter = 0
        self.indentation = 0
        self.svg_depth = 0
        self.element_stack: List[DOMElement] = []
        self.has_svg = False
        self.stylesheet_sources: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (var_name, css_content)
        self.options: Set[str] = set()

    def _next_var(self) -> str:
        self.unnamed_element_counter += 1
        return f"element_{self.unnamed_element_counter}"

    def _current_parent(self) -> str:
        if self.element_stack:
            return self.element_stack[-1].var_name
        return "parent"

    def _deref_parent(self) -> str:
        current_parent = self._current_parent()
        if len(self.element_stack) > 0:
            return f"{current_parent}->"
        return f"{current_parent}."

    def _add_line(self, line: str) -> None:
        if not line.strip():
            self.lines.append("")
            return
        self.lines.append(("    " * self.indentation) + line)

    def handle_starttag(self, tag: str, attrs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]]) -> None:
        self._handle_tag(tag, attrs, self_closing=False)

    def handle_startendtag(self, tag: str, attrs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]]) -> None:
        self._handle_tag(tag, attrs, self_closing=True)

    def _handle_tag(self, tag: str, attrs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]], self_closing: bool) -> None:
        attribute_dict = dict(attrs)

        # Wrap optional nodes in if statements
        option = attribute_dict.pop("data-option", None)
        if option:
            option = to_pascal_case(option)
            self._add_line(f"if (has_flag(options, {self.struct_name}::Options::{option})) {{")
            self.indentation += 1
            self.options.add(option)
        else:
            option = None

        # Handle SVG contexts
        in_svg = self.svg_depth > 0
        if tag == "svg":
            self.svg_depth += 1
            in_svg = True
            self.has_svg = True

        # Handle <link rel="stylesheet"> specially
        if tag == "link":
            assert attribute_dict.get("rel") is not None
            assert "href" in attribute_dict
            self._handle_stylesheet_link(attribute_dict)
            return

        # Determine variable name
        data_name = attribute_dict.pop("data-name", None)
        if data_name:
            var_name = to_snake_case(data_name)
            self.named_fields.append(var_name)
            is_named = True
        else:
            var_name = self._next_var()
            is_named = False

        namespace_expr, tag_expr = resolve_tag(tag, in_svg, self.html_tags, self.svg_tags)
        deref_parent = self._deref_parent()

        self._add_line(f"auto {var_name} = MUST(DOM::create_element(document, {tag_expr}, {namespace_expr}));")
        if is_named:
            self._add_line(f"this->{var_name} = {var_name};")

        # Set attributes (skip data-name)
        for attribute_name, attribute_value in attribute_dict.items():
            if attribute_value is None:
                attribute_value = ""
            attribute_expr = resolve_attribute(attribute_name, in_svg, self.html_attributes, self.svg_attributes)
            self._add_line(f'{var_name}->set_attribute_value({attribute_expr}, "{attribute_value}"_utf16);')

        self._add_line(f"MUST({deref_parent}append_child({var_name}));")

        self._add_line("")

        self.element_stack.append(DOMElement(var_name, tag, option))

        if self_closing or (tag in HTML_VOID_ELEMENTS and not in_svg):
            self.handle_endtag(tag)

    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
        if self.element_stack and self.element_stack[-1].tag == tag:
            node = self.element_stack.pop()

            if tag == "svg":
                self.svg_depth -= 1
            if node.option:
                self.indentation -= 1
                if not self.lines[-1]:
                    self.lines.pop()
                self._add_line(f"}} // Options::{node.option}")
                self._add_line("")

    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
        if data.strip():
            deref_parent = self._deref_parent()
            self._add_line(f'MUST({deref_parent}set_text_content(R"~~~({data})~~~"_utf16));')
            self._add_line("")

    def handle_comment(self, data: str) -> None:
        pass

    def _handle_stylesheet_link(self, attribute_dict: Dict[str, Optional[str]]) -> None:
        href = attribute_dict["href"]
        assert href is not None
        css_path = os.path.join(self.input_dir, href)
        with open(css_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            css_content = f.read()

        assert attribute_dict.get("data-name") is None
        var_name = self._next_var()

        source_var = f"s_stylesheet_source_{len(self.stylesheet_sources) + 1}"
        self.stylesheet_sources.append((source_var, css_content))

        deref_parent = self._deref_parent()

        self._add_line(
            f"auto {var_name} = MUST(DOM::create_element(document, HTML::TagNames::style, Namespace::HTML));"
        )
        self._add_line(f"MUST({var_name}->set_text_content(Utf16String::from_utf8({source_var})));")
        self._add_line(f"MUST({deref_parent}append_child({var_name}));")

        self._add_line("")


def generate(
    input_html: str,
    struct_name: str,
    namespace: str,
    header_path: str,
    html_tags_path: str,
    html_attributes_path: str,
    svg_tags_path: str,
    svg_attributes_path: str,
) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    html_tags = parse_html_tag_header(html_tags_path)
    html_attributes = parse_html_attribute_header(html_attributes_path)
    svg_tags = parse_svg_tag_header(svg_tags_path)
    svg_attributes = parse_svg_attribute_header(svg_attributes_path)

    input_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(input_html))
    with open(input_html, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        html_content = f.read()

    parser = DOMTreeParser(struct_name, html_tags, html_attributes, svg_tags, svg_attributes, input_dir)
    parser.feed(html_content)

    if not parser.lines[-1]:
        parser.lines.pop()

    # Generate header
    header_lines: List[str] = []
    header_lines.append("#pragma once")
    header_lines.append("")
    if parser.options:
        header_lines.append("#include <AK/EnumBits.h>")
    header_lines.append("#include <LibGC/Weak.h>")
    header_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/Forward.h>")
    header_lines.append("")
    header_lines.append(f"namespace {namespace} {{")
    header_lines.append("")
    header_lines.append(f"struct {struct_name} {{")

    if parser.options:
        header_lines.append(f"    enum class Options : u{bits_for_count(len(parser.options))} {{")
        header_lines.append("        None = 0,")
        option_bit = 0
        for option in parser.options:
            header_lines.append(f"        {option} = 1 << {option_bit},")
            option_bit += 1
        header_lines.append("    };")
        header_lines.append("")

    header_lines.append(
        f"    {struct_name}(DOM::Document&, DOM::Node& parent{(', Options = Options::None' if parser.options else '')});"
    )
    header_lines.append("")
    for field in parser.named_fields:
        header_lines.append(f"    GC::Weak<DOM::Element> {field};")
    header_lines.append("};")
    header_lines.append("")
    if parser.options:
        header_lines.append(f"AK_ENUM_BITWISE_OPERATORS({struct_name}::Options);")
        header_lines.append("")
    header_lines.append(f"}} // namespace {namespace}")
    header_lines.append("")

    # Generate implementation
    impl_lines: List[str] = []

    impl_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/DOM/Document.h>")
    impl_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/DOM/ElementFactory.h>")
    impl_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/HTML/AttributeNames.h>")
    impl_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/HTML/TagNames.h>")
    impl_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/Namespace.h>")
    if parser.has_svg:
        impl_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/SVG/AttributeNames.h>")
        impl_lines.append("#include <LibWeb/SVG/TagNames.h>")
    impl_lines.append("")

    impl_lines.append(f'#include "{header_path}"')
    impl_lines.append("")

    impl_lines.append(f"namespace {namespace} {{")
    impl_lines.append("")

    # Static stylesheet sources
    for source_var, css_content in parser.stylesheet_sources:
        impl_lines.append(f'static String const& {source_var} = *new String(R"~~~(')
        impl_lines.append(css_content.strip())
        impl_lines.append(')~~~"_string);')
        impl_lines.append("")

    # Constructor
    impl_lines.append(
        f"{struct_name}::{struct_name}(DOM::Document& document, DOM::Node& parent{', Options options' if parser.options else ''})"
    )
    impl_lines.append("{")
    for line in parser.lines:
        if line:
            impl_lines.append(f"    {line}")
        else:
            impl_lines.append("")
    impl_lines.append("}")
    impl_lines.append("")
    impl_lines.append(f"}} // namespace {namespace}")
    impl_lines.append("")

    return "\n".join(header_lines), "\n".join(impl_lines)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate C++ DOM tree from HTML template", add_help=False)
    parser.add_argument("-h", required=True, dest="header_output")
    parser.add_argument("-c", required=True, dest="impl_output")
    parser.add_argument("-i", required=True, dest="input_html")
    parser.add_argument("-s", required=True, dest="struct_name")
    parser.add_argument("-n", required=True, dest="namespace")
    parser.add_argument("--html-tags", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--html-attributes", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--svg-tags", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--svg-attributes", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    header_path = os.path.relpath(args.header_output, os.path.dirname(str(args.impl_output)))
    if header_path.endswith(".tmp"):
        header_path = header_path[:-4]

    header, impl = generate(
        args.input_html,
        args.struct_name,
        args.namespace,
        header_path,
        args.html_tags,
        args.html_attributes,
        args.svg_tags,
        args.svg_attributes,
    )

    with open(args.header_output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(header)

    with open(args.impl_output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(impl)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

FILE: Meta/Generators/generate_hsts_preload_data.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3

# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

import argparse
import ipaddress
import json
import re

from pathlib import Path

NAME_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9.-]+")

INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS_BIT = 1 << 31


def parse_entries(input_path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, bool]]:
    text = input_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    # Chromium's transport_security_state_static.json uses // line comments, which are not legal JSON.
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*//.*$", "", text)

    data = json.loads(text)
    raw_entries = data["entries"]

    result: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []
    for entry in raw_entries:
        if entry.get("mode") != "force-https":
            continue

        name = entry["name"]

        try:
            ipaddress.ip_address(name)
            continue
        except ValueError:
            pass

        name = name.lower()
        if not NAME_RE.fullmatch(name):
            raise ValueError(
                f"HSTS preload entry name {name!r} contains characters outside [a-z0-9.-]; "
                f"refusing to emit it as a C++ string literal without an explicit policy."
            )

        include_subdomains = bool(entry.get("include_subdomains", False))
        result.append((name, include_subdomains))

    result.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[0])

    seen: set[str] = set()
    for name, _ in result:
        if name in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate HSTS preload entry: {name!r}")
        seen.add(name)

    return result


def generate_header_file(output_path: Path) -> None:
    content = """#pragma once

#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/StringView.h>

namespace HTTP {

struct HSTSPreloadEntry {
    StringView name;
    bool include_subdomains;
};

class HSTSPreloadData {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(HSTSPreloadData);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(HSTSPreloadData);

public:
    static HSTSPreloadData const& the();

    Optional<HSTSPreloadEntry> find_exact(StringView lowercased_domain) const;
    bool is_known_preloaded_hsts_host(StringView domain) const;

private:
    HSTSPreloadData() = default;
};

}
"""
    output_path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")


def generate_implementation_file(entries: list[tuple[str, bool]], output_path: Path) -> None:
    # NB: The names are one string and each entry is where its name starts in it, so the table holds no pointers. A table
    #     of pointers would need a relocation per entry, which dirties every page of it in every process.
    offsets: list[int] = []
    offset = 0
    for name, include_subdomains in entries:
        offsets.append(offset | (INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS_BIT if include_subdomains else 0))
        offset += len(name)
    offsets.append(offset)
    if offset >= INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS_BIT:
        raise ValueError("HSTS preload entry names do not fit in the offsets of the generated table")

    lines: list[str] = []
    lines.append("#include <AK/Array.h>")
    lines.append("#include <AK/StringView.h>")
    lines.append("#include <LibHTTP/HSTSPreloadData.h>")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("namespace HTTP {")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("static constexpr char s_hsts_preload_names[] =")
    for name, _ in entries:
        lines.append(f'    "{name}"')
    lines.append("    ;")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"static constexpr u32 include_subdomains_bit = {INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS_BIT:#x};")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        "// Where each entry's name starts in the names, with include_subdomains_bit set where the entry includes its"
    )
    lines.append("// subdomains, and a last offset where the names end.")
    lines.append(f"static constexpr Array<u32, {len(offsets)}> s_hsts_preload_offsets {{ {{")
    for chunk_start in range(0, len(offsets), 8):
        chunk = offsets[chunk_start : chunk_start + 8]
        lines.append("    " + " ".join(f"{value:#x}," for value in chunk))
    lines.append("} };")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("static StringView name_of_entry(size_t index)")
    lines.append("{")
    lines.append("    auto start = s_hsts_preload_offsets[index] & ~include_subdomains_bit;")
    lines.append("    auto end = s_hsts_preload_offsets[index + 1] & ~include_subdomains_bit;")
    lines.append("    return { s_hsts_preload_names + start, end - start };")
    lines.append("}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("HSTSPreloadData const& HSTSPreloadData::the()")
    lines.append("{")
    lines.append("    static HSTSPreloadData s_the;")
    lines.append("    return s_the;")
    lines.append("}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("Optional<HSTSPreloadEntry> HSTSPreloadData::find_exact(StringView needle) const")
    lines.append("{")
    lines.append("    size_t low = 0;")
    lines.append("    size_t high = s_hsts_preload_offsets.size() - 1;")
    lines.append("    while (low < high) {")
    lines.append("        auto middle = low + (high - low) / 2;")
    lines.append("        auto name = name_of_entry(middle);")
    lines.append("        auto comparison = needle.compare(name);")
    lines.append("        if (comparison == 0)")
    lines.append(
        "            return HSTSPreloadEntry { name, (s_hsts_preload_offsets[middle] & include_subdomains_bit) != 0 };"
    )
    lines.append("        if (comparison < 0)")
    lines.append("            high = middle;")
    lines.append("        else")
    lines.append("            low = middle + 1;")
    lines.append("    }")
    lines.append("    return {};")
    lines.append("}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797#section-8.2")
    lines.append("bool HSTSPreloadData::is_known_preloaded_hsts_host(StringView domain) const")
    lines.append("{")
    lines.append("    if (find_exact(domain).has_value())")
    lines.append("        return true;")
    lines.append("    auto remaining = domain;")
    lines.append("    while (true) {")
    lines.append("        auto dot = remaining.find('.');")
    lines.append("        if (!dot.has_value())")
    lines.append("            break;")
    lines.append("        remaining = remaining.substring_view(*dot + 1);")
    lines.append("        if (auto entry = find_exact(remaining); entry.has_value() && entry->include_subdomains)")
    lines.append("            return true;")
    lines.append("    }")
    lines.append("    return false;")
    lines.append("}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("}")
    lines.append("")

    output_path.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate HSTS preload data files", add_help=False)
    parser.add_argument("--help", action="help", help="Show this help message and exit")
    parser.add_argument("-h", "--generated-header-path", required=True, help="Path to the header file to generate")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c", "--generated-implementation-path", required=True, help="Path to the implementation file to generate"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-p",
        "--hsts-preload-list-path",
        required=True,
        help="Path to Chromium's transport_security_state_static.json",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    entries = parse_entries(Path(args.hsts_preload_list_path))
    generate_header_file(Path(args.generated_header_path))
    generate_implementation_file(entries, Path(args.generated_implementation_path))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

@dataclass
class Parameter:
    attributes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    type: str = ""
    type_for_encoding: str = ""
    name: str = ""
    # The value an enum's declaration gives the member.
    value: Optional[int] = None


@dataclass
class Message:
    attributes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    name: str = ""
    is_synchronous: bool = False
    inputs: List[Parameter] = field(default_factory=list)
    outputs: List[Parameter] = field(default_factory=list)

    def response_name(self) -> str:
        return f"{pascal_case(self.name)}Response"

    def is_received_in_rust(self) -> bool:
        return "RustReceiver" in self.attributes

    def is_sent_from_rust(self) -> bool:
        return "RustSender" in self.attributes

    def has_cpp_class(self) -> bool:
        return not (self.is_received_in_rust() and self.is_sent_from_rust())


@dataclass
class Endpoint:
    name: str = ""
    magic: int = 0
    messages: List[Message] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The argument a message can be routed by: messages whose first parameter is this one are about the
    # object it names, so a receiver can hand them to that object and a sender can bind a proxy to it.
    route: Optional[Parameter] = None
    export_macro: str = ""

    def binds(self, message: Message) -> bool:
        if self.route is None or not message.inputs:
            return False
        return message.inputs[0].type == self.route.type and message.inputs[0].name == self.route.name

    def routes(self, message: Message) -> bool:
        # A message the connection answers itself stays on the connection, whatever it starts with. It is still
        # bound: what the receiver does with a message says nothing about how a sender names its object.
        if "NotRouted" in message.attributes:
            return False
        return self.binds(message)

    def has_messages_received_in_rust(self) -> bool:
        return any(message.is_received_in_rust() for message in self.messages)

    def names_rust_for_some_message(self) -> bool:
        return any(message.is_received_in_rust() or message.is_sent_from_rust() for message in self.messages)

    def validate(self) -> None:
        if self.route is None:
            return
        if self.names_rust_for_some_message():
            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.name} is routed, so its messages cannot be [RustReceiver] or [RustSender]")
        for message in self.messages:
            if not self.routes(message):
                continue
            # A routed message whose object is gone is dropped, and a synchronous sender waits for an answer. An
            # empty one acknowledges; one carrying values would be invented, and the zero of a type is an answer.
            if message.is_synchronous and message.outputs:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"{self.name}::{message.name} is synchronous and returns values, so it cannot be routed: "
                    f"mark it [NotRouted] and answer it on the connection"
                )

    def route_scope(self) -> str:
        assert self.route is not None
        name = self.route.name
        if name.endswith("_id"):
            name = name[: -len("_id")]
        return name

    def route_scope_pascal(self) -> str:
        return pascal_case(self.route_scope())


INTEGER_TYPES = {"u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "i8", "i16", "i32", "i64"}

# The attributes a struct field may have, and the types each one applies to.
FIELD_ATTRIBUTE_TYPES = {
    "MaxBytes": {"String", "ByteString", "ByteBuffer"},
    "MaxCount": {"Vector"},
    "NonZero": INTEGER_TYPES,
    "Finite": {"float", "double"},
}

IDENTIFIER = r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*"
QUALIFIED_NAME = re.compile(rf"{IDENTIFIER}(::{IDENTIFIER})*")
FIELD_TYPE = re.compile(rf"(::)?{IDENTIFIER}(::{IDENTIFIER})*(<.+>)?")

# Spellings of the same C++ type, which must not be told apart.
TYPE_ALIASES = {"int": "i32", "unsigned": "u32", "size_t": "u64"}


def canonical_type(type: str) -> str:
    """The type with one spelling for each C++ type: without leading "::", and with sized integer names."""
    type = re.sub(r"(?<![\w:])::", "", type)
    type = re.sub(r"\bunsigned int\b", "u32", type)
    return re.sub(r"(?<![\w:])\w+(?![\w:])", lambda name: TYPE_ALIASES.get(name[0], name[0]), type)


def field_attributes(member: Parameter) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    """The attributes of a struct field as (name, argument) pairs, e.g. ("MaxBytes", "64")."""
    attributes: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    for attribute in member.attributes:
        name, _, argument = attribute.partition("=")
        attributes.append((name.strip(), argument.strip()))
    return attributes


@dataclass
class FieldRefusal:
    """A value of a field that its attributes refuse: how C++ and Rust find it, and what is wrong with it."""

    attribute: str
    cpp_condition: str
    rust_condition: str
    meaning: str

    def is_checked_after_decoding(self) -> bool:
        # NB: Decoders check sizes before they decode the contents.
        return self.attribute not in ("MaxBytes", "MaxCount")


def field_refusals(member: Parameter, cpp_value: str, rust_value: str) -> List[FieldRefusal]:
    refusals: List[FieldRefusal] = []
    for name, argument in field_attributes(member):
        if name == "NonZero":
            refusals.append(FieldRefusal(name, f"{cpp_value} == 0", f"{rust_value} == 0", "is zero"))
        elif name == "Finite":
            refusals.append(
                FieldRefusal(name, f"!isfinite({cpp_value})", f"!{rust_value}.is_finite()", "is not finite")
            )
        elif name in ("MaxBytes", "MaxCount"):
            cpp_size = {"String": "bytes().size()", "ByteString": "length()"}.get(member.type, "size()")
            rust_size = {"String": "as_bytes().len()", "ByteString": "0.len()"}.get(member.type, "len()")
            refusals.append(
                FieldRefusal(
                    name,
                    f"{cpp_value}.{cpp_size} > {argument}",
                    f"{rust_value}.{rust_size} > {argument}",
                    "is too large",
                )
            )
    return refusals


@dataclass
class Declaration:
    """A type declared in an IPC file: a struct, an enum or a variant."""

    kind: str = ""
    # The C++ name, including its namespace, e.g. "WebView::DictionaryLookup".
    name: str = ""
    attributes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The integer type an enum goes as.
    underlying_type: str = ""
    # A struct's fields, an enum's values (by name, or all of them with the numbers C++ gives them), or a variant's
    # alternatives (with a name for Rust).
    members: List[Parameter] = field(default_factory=list)

    def is_existing_cpp(self) -> bool:
        # The C++ type is defined elsewhere, so only its codec is generated.
        # NB: Nothing can check that the declaration of an existing struct lists every field of its C++ type, so a
        #     field it leaves out is not sent, and the decoder leaves it to its default. The declaration must list
        #     them all, in their C++ order.
        return "ExistingCpp" in self.attributes

    def rust_name(self) -> str:
        return self.name.replace("::", "_")

    def has_accessors(self) -> bool:
        # The existing C++ type is read through accessor functions and built with a constructor taking every field.
        return "Accessors" in self.attributes

    def gives_values(self) -> bool:
        # The enum goes as the number of its value rather than as the value's position in the declaration.
        return self.kind == "enum" and self.members[0].value is not None

    def is_flags(self) -> bool:
        # The enum's values are bits, and any combination of them goes, as the number it is.
        return "Flags" in self.attributes

    def rust_derives(self) -> List[str]:
        derives = ["Clone", "Copy", "Debug", "PartialEq", "Eq"]
        if self.kind != "enum":
            carries_a_file = any("IPC::File" in member.type for member in self.members)
            derives = [] if carries_a_file else ["Clone", "Debug", "PartialEq"]
        for attribute in self.attributes:
            name, _, argument = attribute.partition("=")
            if name == "RustDerive":
                derives += [derive for derive in argument.split("+") if derive not in derives]
        return derives

    def validate(self) -> None:
        if not re.fullmatch(rf"{IDENTIFIER}(::{IDENTIFIER})+", self.name):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Expected a type name with a namespace, got '{self.name}'")
        for attribute in self.attributes:
            name, _, argument = attribute.partition("=")
            if name == "RustDerive":
                if not re.fullmatch(rf"{IDENTIFIER}(\+{IDENTIFIER})*", argument):
                    raise RuntimeError(f"RustDerive on {self.name} needs traits joined by '+', got '{argument}'")
            elif attribute not in ("ExistingCpp", "Accessors", "Flags"):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Unknown attribute '{attribute}' on {self.name}")
        if self.has_accessors() and (self.kind != "struct" or not self.is_existing_cpp()):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Only an existing C++ struct can have accessors: {self.name}")
        if self.is_flags() and self.kind != "enum":
            raise RuntimeError(f"Only an enum can be flags: {self.name}")

        names = [member.name for member in self.members]
        for name in names:
            if not re.fullmatch(IDENTIFIER, name):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid member name '{name}' in {self.name}")
        if self.kind != "enum":
            for member in self.members:
                if not FIELD_TYPE.fullmatch(member.type):
                    raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid type '{member.type}' of {self.name}::{member.name}")
        if len(set(names)) != len(names):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Duplicate member name in {self.name}")
        if self.kind != "struct" and not names:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Empty {self.kind}: {self.name}")

        if self.kind == "enum":
            if self.underlying_type not in INTEGER_TYPES:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Enum {self.name} needs a sized integer type, got '{self.underlying_type}'")
            is_signed = self.underlying_type.startswith("i")
            value_bits = int(self.underlying_type[1:]) - (1 if is_signed else 0)
            if len(names) > 2**value_bits:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Enum {self.name} has more values than {self.underlying_type} holds")
            values = [member.value for member in self.members if member.value is not None]
            if values and len(values) != len(names):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Enum {self.name} needs a value for each of its members or for none")
            if self.is_flags() and not values:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Flags {self.name} need a value for each of their members")
            for value in values:
                if not (-(2**value_bits) if is_signed else 0) <= value < 2**value_bits:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"Enum {self.name} has a value that {self.underlying_type} does not hold")
            if not self.is_flags() and len(set(values)) != len(values):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Duplicate value in {self.name}")
        elif self.kind == "variant":
            # NB: An AK::Variant of fewer than 255 types goes with a u8 index.
            if len(names) >= 255:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Variant {self.name} has too many alternatives")
            if len({canonical_type(member.type) for member in self.members}) != len(self.members):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Variant {self.name} needs a distinct type for each alternative")
        else:
            for member in self.members:
                for name, argument in field_attributes(member):
                    if name not in FIELD_ATTRIBUTE_TYPES:
                        raise RuntimeError(f"Unknown attribute '{name}' on {self.name}::{member.name}")
                    if member.type.partition("<")[0] not in FIELD_ATTRIBUTE_TYPES[name]:
                        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} cannot apply to {self.name}::{member.name} of type {member.type}")
                    if name in ("MaxBytes", "MaxCount"):
                        if not argument.isdecimal() or not 0 < int(argument) <= 0xFFFFFFFF:
                            raise RuntimeError(f"{name} on {self.name}::{member.name} needs a size, got '{argument}'")
                    elif argument:
                        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} on {self.name}::{member.name} takes no argument")


@dataclass
class Document:
    includes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    declarations: List[Declaration] = field(default_factory=list)
    endpoints: List[Endpoint] = field(default_factory=list)


def is_primitive_type(type: str) -> bool:
    return type in PRIMITIVE_TYPES


def is_simple_type(type: str) -> bool:
    if type.startswith("ReadonlySpan<") and type.endswith(">"):
        return True
    return type in SIMPLE_TYPES


def is_primitive_or_simple_type(type: str) -> bool:
    return is_primitive_type(type) or is_simple_type(type)


def pascal_case(identifier: str) -> str:
    words = identifier.split("_")
    return "".join(word[0].title() + word[1:] for word in words)


def message_name_qualified(endpoint: str, message: str, is_response: bool) -> str:
    message = pascal_case(message)
    response = "Response" if is_response else ""

    return f"Messages::{endpoint}::{message}{response}"


def make_argument_type(type: str) -> str:
    if is_primitive_or_simple_type(type):
        return type
    return f"{type} const&"


def parse(contents: str) -> Document:
    lexer = Lexer(contents)
    document = Document()
    endpoints = document.endpoints

    def assert_specific(ch: str) -> None:
        if not lexer.consume_specific(ch):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Expected '{ch}' at position {lexer.position}, got '{lexer.peek()}'")

    def consume_whitespace() -> None:
        lexer.ignore_while(lambda c: c.isspace())
        while lexer.next_is("//"):
            lexer.ignore_until("\n")
            lexer.ignore_while(lambda c: c.isspace())

    def parse_parameter_type(delimiters: str = "") -> str:
        parameter_type = lexer.consume_until(lambda c: c == "<" or c.isspace() or c in delimiters)

        if lexer.peek() == "<":
            lexer.consume()

            parts: List[str] = [parameter_type, "<"]
            nesting = 1

            while nesting > 0:
                inner = lexer.consume_until(lambda c: c in ("<", ">"))
                if lexer.is_eof():
                    raise RuntimeError("Unexpected EOF when parsing parameter type")

                parts.append(inner)

                if lexer.peek() == "<":
                    nesting += 1
                elif lexer.peek() == ">":
                    nesting -= 1

                parts.append(lexer.consume())

            parameter_type = "".join(parts)

        return parameter_type

    def parse_attributes(storage: List[str]) -> None:
        if not lexer.consume_specific("["):
            return

        while True:
            if lexer.is_eof():
                raise RuntimeError("Unexpected EOF in attributes")

            if lexer.consume_specific("]"):
                consume_whitespace()
                break

            if lexer.consume_specific(","):
                consume_whitespace()

            storage.append(lexer.consume_until(lambda c: c in ("]", ",")).strip())
            consume_whitespace()

    def parse_parameter(storage: List[Parameter], message_name: str) -> None:
        if lexer.is_eof():
            raise RuntimeError("EOF when parsing parameter")

        parameter = Parameter()
