# The Rust types of IDL values, for the Rust bindings of the interfaces implemented in Rust. They cover the types that
# those interfaces use so far; every other type is an error.

import re

from collections.abc import Iterable
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import FrozenSet
from typing import List
from typing import Optional

from Generators.libweb_bindings.context import GenerationContext
from Utils.utils import string_to_cpp_enum_name
from Utils.utils import title_case_to_snake_case
from Utils.webidl_parser import Dictionary
from Utils.webidl_parser import Enumeration
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLParameterizedType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLUnionType
from Utils.webidl_parser import Interface
from Utils.webidl_parser import OperationParameter

# The typed arrays, whose names are the variants of the runtime's TypedArrayKind.
TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES = {
    "Int8Array",
    "Uint8Array",
    "Uint8ClampedArray",
    "Int16Array",
    "Uint16Array",
    "Int32Array",
    "Uint32Array",
    "BigInt64Array",
    "BigUint64Array",
    "Float16Array",
    "Float32Array",
    "Float64Array",
}

# The extended attributes of a type or a parameter that the Rust bindings handle.
SUPPORTED_TYPE_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES = {
    "AllowShared",
    "AllowResizable",
    "Clamp",
    "EnforceRange",
    "LegacyNullToEmptyString",
}

# The integer types, with the Rust type of their values.
INTEGER_TYPES = {
    "short": "i16",
    "unsigned short": "u16",
    "long": "i32",
    "unsigned long": "u32",
    "long long": "i64",
    "unsigned long long": "u64",
}

# The floating point types, with the Rust type of their values.
FLOATING_POINT_TYPES = {"float": "f32", "unrestricted float": "f32", "double": "f64", "unrestricted double": "f64"}

# The types whose values are plain data, with the Rust type of their values. None of these Rust types is or holds a
# cell, which holds_cells() relies on.
PLAIN_DATA_TYPES = {
    "ByteString": "ByteString",
    "CSSOMString": "Utf16String",
    "DOMString": "Utf16String",
    "USVString": "UsvString",
    "boolean": "bool",
    "undefined": "()",
    **INTEGER_TYPES,
    **FLOATING_POINT_TYPES,
}

# The unions that the bindings runtime has a type for, by the name of the typedef that names the union.
RUNTIME_UNION_TYPES = {"ArrayBufferView": "ArrayBufferView", "BufferSource": "BufferSource"}

# The unions that no typedef names and more than one interface's IDL uses, whose enums the bindings runtime defines,
# by their type name.
SHARED_UNNAMED_UNIONS = {"DOMStringOrDOMStringSequence": "crate::bindings::conversions"}

DECIMAL_LITERAL = re.compile(r"-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?")

# https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#prod-integer
INTEGER_LITERAL = re.compile(r"-?([1-9][0-9]*|0[Xx][0-9A-Fa-f]+|0[0-7]*)")


class UnsupportedByRustBindings(Exception):
    pass


def idl_integer_value(literal: Optional[str], idl_type_name: str) -> Optional[int]:
    """The value of an integer token of the IDL, or None if the token is not one or its value is not one of the
    integer type."""
    if literal is None or not INTEGER_LITERAL.fullmatch(literal):
        return None
    digits = literal.removeprefix("-")
    if digits[:2] in ("0x", "0X"):
        magnitude = int(digits, 16)
    elif digits.startswith("0"):
        magnitude = int(digits, 8)
    else:
        magnitude = int(digits, 10)
    integer = -magnitude if literal.startswith("-") else magnitude
    rust_integer_type = INTEGER_TYPES[idl_type_name]
    bits = int(rust_integer_type[1:])
    if rust_integer_type.startswith("u"):
        lowest, highest = 0, 2**bits - 1
    else:
        lowest, highest = -(2 ** (bits - 1)), 2 ** (bits - 1) - 1
    if not lowest <= integer <= highest:
        return None
    return integer


def rust_integer_literal(literal: Optional[str], idl_type_name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """The Rust literal of the value of an integer token of the IDL, if it is a value of the integer type."""
    integer = idl_integer_value(literal, idl_type_name)
    return None if integer is None else f"{integer}_{INTEGER_TYPES[idl_type_name]}"


def is_implemented_in_rust(interface: Optional[Interface]) -> bool:
    return interface is not None and interface.extended_attributes.get("ImplementedIn") == "Rust"


def is_member_implemented_in_rust(member) -> bool:
    """Whether an attribute or an operation of an interface implemented in C++ is [ImplementedIn=Rust]: its bindings
    and its steps are Rust code, which the C++ bindings call to define it on the interface prototype object."""
    return member.extended_attributes.get("ImplementedIn") == "Rust"


def rust_member_definition_entry_point(interface: Interface, member) -> str:
    """The entry point of the Rust bindings that defines an [ImplementedIn=Rust] member of an interface implemented in
    C++ on its interface prototype object."""
    return f"web_rust_{title_case_to_snake_case(interface.name)}_define_{title_case_to_snake_case(member.name)}"


def rust_implemented_members(interface: Optional[Interface]) -> Optional[Interface]:
    """The interface implemented in C++ with only its members that are [ImplementedIn=Rust], without that extended
    attribute, which is what the Rust bindings write bindings for. None if it has no such member."""
    if interface is None or is_implemented_in_rust(interface):
        return None
    attributes = [attribute for attribute in interface.regular_attributes if is_member_implemented_in_rust(attribute)]
    operations = [operation for operation in interface.regular_operations if is_member_implemented_in_rust(operation)]
    if not attributes and not operations:
        return None

    def without_implemented_in(member):
        extended_attributes = dict(member.extended_attributes)
        del extended_attributes["ImplementedIn"]
        return replace(member, extended_attributes=extended_attributes)

    return replace(
        interface,
        extended_attributes={},
        parent_name="",
        constants=[],
        regular_attributes=[without_implemented_in(attribute) for attribute in attributes],
        static_attributes=[],
        regular_operations=[without_implemented_in(operation) for operation in operations],
        static_operations=[],
        constructors=[],
        stringifier=None,
        iterable=None,
        async_iterable=None,
        named_property_getter=None,
        indexed_property_getter=None,
        named_property_setter=None,
        named_property_deleter=None,
        indexed_property_setter=None,
        maplike=None,
        setlike=None,
    )


# The interfaces implemented in C++ that an interface implemented in Rust can inherit from
# (Libraries/LibWeb/Bindings/RustEventTarget.h).
CPP_PARENT_INTERFACES = ("EventTarget", "Event")


def cpp_ancestor(interface: Interface, context: GenerationContext) -> Optional[Interface]:
    """The interface implemented in C++ that the interface inherits from, through any number of interfaces
    implemented in Rust, if any."""
    ancestor = context.interfaces.get(interface.parent_name)
    while ancestor is not None and is_implemented_in_rust(ancestor):
        ancestor = context.interfaces.get(ancestor.parent_name)
    return ancestor


def resolved_dictionary(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> Optional[Dictionary]:
    return context.dictionaries.get(idl_type.name)


def rust_interface(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> Optional[Interface]:
    """The interface that the type names, if it is implemented in Rust."""
    if isinstance(idl_type, (IDLParameterizedType, IDLUnionType)):
        return None
    interface = context.interfaces.get(idl_type.name)
    return interface if is_implemented_in_rust(interface) else None


def rust_module_path(idl_path: Path) -> str:
    """The Rust module of the hand-written definitions of an IDL file, which follows from its path:
    Encoding/TextEncoder.idl names crate::encoding::text_encoder."""
    parts = idl_path.parts
    namespace = parts[parts.index("LibWeb") + 1]
    module = "webidl" if namespace == "WebIDL" else title_case_to_snake_case(namespace)
    return f"crate::{module}::{title_case_to_snake_case(idl_path.stem)}"


def cpp_interface(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> Optional[Interface]:
    """The interface that the type names, if LibWeb implements it in C++."""
    if isinstance(idl_type, (IDLParameterizedType, IDLUnionType)):
        return None
    interface = context.interfaces.get(idl_type.name)
    if interface is None or is_implemented_in_rust(interface):
        return None
    if interface.is_namespace or interface.is_callback_interface:
        return None
    return interface


def is_window_proxy(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
    """Whether the type is WindowProxy, which no IDL file defines. Rust holds its values as the objects that scripts
    see."""
    return not isinstance(idl_type, (IDLParameterizedType, IDLUnionType)) and idl_type.name == "WindowProxy"


def is_callback_interface(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    """Whether the type names a callback interface."""
    if isinstance(idl_type, (IDLParameterizedType, IDLUnionType)):
        return False
    interface = context.interfaces.get(idl_type.name)
    return interface is not None and interface.is_callback_interface


def cpp_interface_name_constant(interface: Interface) -> str:
    """The constant of the generated Rust bindings that is the Web::Bindings::InterfaceName of an interface that
    LibWeb implements in C++."""
    return f"super::cpp_interface_names::{title_case_to_snake_case(interface.name).upper()}"


def is_union_of_cpp_interfaces(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    return isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType) and all(
        cpp_interface(member_type, context) is not None for member_type in idl_type.flattened_member_types()
    )


def inheriting_interfaces(interface: Interface, context: GenerationContext) -> List[Interface]:
    """The interfaces that inherit from the interface, through any number of interfaces between them."""
    inheriting = []
    for other in context.interfaces.values():
        ancestor = context.interfaces.get(other.parent_name)
        while ancestor is not None and ancestor.name != interface.name:
            ancestor = context.interfaces.get(ancestor.parent_name)
        if ancestor is not None:
            inheriting.append(other)
    return inheriting


def rust_interface_path(interface: Interface) -> str:
    """The Rust path of the implementation of an interface: crate::encoding::text_encoder::TextEncoder for
    Encoding/TextEncoder.idl."""
    return f"{rust_module_path(interface.path)}::{interface.name}"


def rust_any_interface_path(interface: Interface) -> str:
    """The Rust path of the enum of an object of an interface that others inherit from, which is an object of the
    interface or of any of those, with a variant for each that is named after its interface:
    crate::file_api::blob::AnyBlob for FileAPI/Blob.idl."""
    return f"{rust_module_path(interface.path)}::Any{interface.name}"


def rust_dictionary_path(dictionary: Dictionary, context: GenerationContext) -> str:
    """The Rust path of the struct of a dictionary, which is in the module of the IDL file that defines the
    dictionary: crate::encoding::text_encoder::TextEncoderEncodeIntoResult."""
    for module in context.modules:
        if any(defined.name == dictionary.name for defined in module.dictionaries):
            return f"{rust_module_path(module.path)}::{dictionary.name}"
    raise RuntimeError(f"No module defines the dictionary {dictionary.name}")


def union_typedef_names(idl_type: IDLUnionType, context: GenerationContext) -> List[str]:
    return sorted(
        name
        for name, typedef in context.typedefs.items()
        if typedef.type.without_nullable() == idl_type.without_nullable()
    )


def is_unnamed_union_of_cpp_interfaces(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    """Whether the IDL values of the union are objects of interfaces that LibWeb implements in C++ and nothing says
    which. Their Rust type is that of such an object, which is all an implementation can do with one: hand it on."""
    return (
        isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType)
        and is_union_of_cpp_interfaces(idl_type, context)
        and not union_typedef_names(idl_type, context)
    )


def idl_type_name(idl_type: IDLType, what: str, context: Optional[GenerationContext] = None) -> str:
    """The name the Rust bindings give the type: Path2DOrDOMString for (Path2D or DOMString),
    UnrestrictedDoubleSequence for sequence<unrestricted double>. Given the context, a member union that one typedef
    names has the typedef's name: DocumentOrXMLHttpRequestBodyInit for (Document or XMLHttpRequestBodyInit)."""
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType):
        if context is not None:
            names = union_typedef_names(idl_type, context)
            if len(names) == 1:
                return f"{names[0]}OrNull" if idl_type.nullable else names[0]
        name = "Or".join(idl_type_name(member_type, what, context) for member_type in idl_type.member_types)
    elif isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType) and idl_type.name == "record":
        key_type, value_type = idl_type.parameters
        name = f"{idl_type_name(key_type, what, context)}{idl_type_name(value_type, what, context)}Record"
    elif isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType):
        if idl_type.name != "sequence":
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has the type {idl_type}, which the Rust bindings have no name for")
        name = f"{idl_type_name(idl_type.parameters[0], what, context)}Sequence"
    else:
        name = "".join(word[:1].upper() + word[1:] for word in idl_type.name.split(" "))
    return f"{name}OrNull" if idl_type.nullable else name


def member_types_of_interface(interface: Interface) -> List[IDLType]:
    """The types that the attributes, operations and constructors of an interface or a mixin name."""
    types = [attribute.type for attribute in interface.regular_attributes + interface.static_attributes]
    for operation in interface.regular_operations + interface.static_operations:
        types.append(operation.return_type)
        types.extend(parameter.type for parameter in operation.parameters)
    for constructor in interface.constructors:
        types.extend(parameter.type for parameter in constructor.parameters)
    return types


def unnamed_union_idl_path(idl_type: IDLUnionType, context: GenerationContext, what: str) -> Path:
    """The IDL file of a union that no typedef names: the file of the mixin, or else of the interface or the
    dictionary, whose members name it. An interface has the members of the mixins that it includes, so a union that
    a mixin names is the mixin's."""
    union_type = idl_type.without_nullable()

    def name_the_union(types: Iterable[IDLType]) -> bool:
        return any(
            nested_type.without_nullable() == union_type
            for named_type in types
            for nested_type in named_type.nested_types()
        )

    paths = {mixin.path for mixin in context.mixins.values() if name_the_union(member_types_of_interface(mixin))}
    if not paths:
        interfaces = []
        for module in context.modules:
            if module.interface is not None and name_the_union(member_types_of_interface(module.interface)):
                paths.add(module.path)
                interfaces.append(module.interface)
            if any(name_the_union(member.type for member in dictionary.members) for dictionary in module.dictionaries):
                paths.add(module.path)
        # NB: A union that an interface and the interfaces that inherit from it name, as the constructors of
        #     DOMMatrixReadOnly and DOMMatrix do, is the union of the interface that the others inherit from.
        roots = [
            interface
            for interface in interfaces
            if all(other is interface or other in inheriting_interfaces(interface, context) for other in interfaces)
        ]
        if len(roots) == 1 and len(paths) == len(interfaces):
            paths = {roots[0].path}
    if len(paths) != 1:
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
            f"{what} has the union type {idl_type}, which no typedef names and which the IDL files "
            f"{sorted(str(path) for path in paths)} name, so that no one module defines its enum"
        )
    return paths.pop()


def runtime_union_type(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> Optional[str]:
    """The type of the bindings runtime for the union, if it has one."""
    if not isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType):
        return None
    for name, runtime_type in RUNTIME_UNION_TYPES.items():
        typedef = context.typedefs.get(name)
        if typedef is not None and typedef.type.without_nullable() == idl_type.without_nullable():
            return runtime_type
    return None


def union_member_types(idl_type: IDLUnionType, context: GenerationContext) -> List[IDLType]:
    """The flattened member types of the union, except that a union the bindings runtime has a type for is one
    member, as BufferSource is in (BufferSource or Blob or USVString)."""
    member_types: List[IDLType] = []
    for member_type in idl_type.member_types:
        if isinstance(member_type, IDLUnionType) and runtime_union_type(member_type, context) is None:
            member_types.extend(union_member_types(member_type, context))
        else:
            member_types.append(member_type)
    return member_types


def member_other_than_undefined(idl_type: IDLType) -> Optional[IDLType]:
    """The other member of a union of a type and undefined, whose IDL values are those of the type or nothing."""
    if not isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType) or idl_type.nullable or len(idl_type.member_types) != 2:
        return None
    others = [member for member in idl_type.member_types if member.name != "undefined"]
    return others[0] if len(others) == 1 else None


def is_named_union(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    """Whether the Rust type of the union is an enum that the module of an IDL file defines, rust_union_path()."""
    return (
        isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType)
        and runtime_union_type(idl_type, context) is None
        and member_other_than_undefined(idl_type) is None
        and not is_unnamed_union_of_cpp_interfaces(idl_type, context)
    )


def rust_union_variant(member_type: IDLType) -> str:
    """The variant of a member of a union in the enum of the union, which has the type name of the member, such as
    DOMString or UnrestrictedDouble. A union has at most one sequence type and one record type, whose variants are
    Sequence and Record."""
    if isinstance(member_type, IDLParameterizedType) and member_type.name == "sequence":
        return "Sequence"
    if isinstance(member_type, IDLParameterizedType) and member_type.name == "record":
        return "Record"
    return idl_type_name(member_type, f"the union member {member_type}")


def rust_enumeration_path(enumeration: Enumeration, context: GenerationContext) -> str:
    """The Rust path of the enum of an enumeration, which is in the module of the IDL file that defines the
    enumeration: crate::web_gl::web_gl_rendering_context::WebGLPowerPreference."""
    return f"{rust_module_path(enumeration.path)}::{enumeration.name}"


def rust_enumeration_variant(value: str, enumeration: Enumeration) -> str:
    """The variant of a value of an enumeration in the enum of the enumeration, which the C++ bindings name the same
    way."""
    variant = string_to_cpp_enum_name(value)
    is_plain = value.isascii() and value.isprintable() and '"' not in value and "\\" not in value
    if not is_plain or not re.fullmatch(r"(?:[A-Z]|_[0-9])[A-Za-z0-9]*", variant) or variant == "Self":
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
            f"The value {value!r} of the enumeration {enumeration.name} has no name that the Rust bindings can give "
            "its variant"
        )
    return variant


def rust_union_path(idl_type: IDLUnionType, context: GenerationContext, what: str) -> str:
    """The Rust path of the enum of a union, which is in the module of the IDL file whose typedef names the union:
    crate::url_pattern::url_pattern::URLPatternInput. The generator resolves typedefs before it converts types, so
    the typedef is found again by its type. A union that no typedef names has its type name, in the module of the
    IDL file that names it: crate::html::path2d::Path2DOrDOMString."""
    names = union_typedef_names(idl_type, context)
    if len(names) > 1:
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has the union type {idl_type}, which the typedefs {names} all name")
    if not names:
        type_name = idl_type_name(idl_type.without_nullable(), what, context)
        if type_name in SHARED_UNNAMED_UNIONS:
            return f"{SHARED_UNNAMED_UNIONS[type_name]}::{type_name}"
        idl_path = unnamed_union_idl_path(idl_type, context, what)
        return f"{rust_module_path(idl_path)}::{type_name}"
    name = names[0]
    for module in context.modules:
        if any(typedef.name == name for typedef in module.typedefs):
            return f"{rust_module_path(module.path)}::{name}"
    raise RuntimeError(f"No module defines the typedef {name}")


def rust_type(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext, what: str, is_result: bool = False) -> str:
    """The Rust type of the IDL values of the type. A result is a value that the implementation returns, which it
    creates, so that it knows the interface of an object it returns."""
    unsupported_attributes = set(idl_type.extended_attributes) - SUPPORTED_TYPE_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES
    if unsupported_attributes:
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has extended attributes {sorted(unsupported_attributes)}")
    if idl_type.nullable:
        return f"Option<{rust_type(idl_type.without_nullable(), context, what, is_result)}>"
    name = idl_type.name
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType):
        if name in ("sequence", "FrozenArray"):
            element_type = idl_type.parameters[0]
            element = rust_type(element_type, context, what, is_result)
            # NB: A Vec would hide cells that the implementation returns from the collector until they are converted.
            if is_result and holds_cells(element_type, context):
                return f"MarkedVec<'_, {element}>"
            return f"Vec<{element}>"
        if name == "Promise":
            return "WebIdlPromise"
        if name == "record":
            key_type, value_type = idl_type.parameters
            if key_type.name not in ("ByteString", "DOMString", "USVString"):
                raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has a record with keys of the type {key_type}")
            return f"Vec<({rust_type(key_type, context, what)}, {rust_type(value_type, context, what)})>"
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has the type {idl_type}, which the Rust bindings do not convert yet")
    if name in PLAIN_DATA_TYPES:
        return PLAIN_DATA_TYPES[name]
    if name == "any":
        return "Value"
    if name == "object":
        return "Gc<Object>"
    if name in TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES:
        return "Gc<TypedArrayBase>"
    if name in ("ArrayBuffer", "SharedArrayBuffer"):
        return "Gc<ArrayBuffer>"
    callback_function = context.callback_function(idl_type)
    if callback_function is not None:
        # NB: A callback function value that the implementation receives keeps its callback context, and one that it
        #     returns is a function that it created.
        if is_result:
            return "Gc<FunctionObject>"
        return "PromiseCallbackFunction" if is_promise_type(callback_function.return_type) else "CallbackFunction"
    if is_callback_interface(idl_type, context) and not is_result:
        return "CallbackInterface"
    interface = rust_interface(idl_type, context)
    if interface is not None:
        if inheriting_interfaces(interface, context) and not is_result:
            # NB: An object of such a type is a cell of any of several classes, which Ref<T> cannot express. An object
            #     that an implementation returns is one of exactly the interface, whose cell it created.
            return rust_any_interface_path(interface)
        return f"Ref<{rust_interface_path(interface)}>"
    if (
        is_window_proxy(idl_type)
        or cpp_interface(idl_type, context) is not None
        or is_unnamed_union_of_cpp_interfaces(idl_type, context)
    ):
        return "CppInterface"
    dictionary = resolved_dictionary(idl_type, context)
    if dictionary is not None:
        return rust_dictionary_type(dictionary, context)
    enumeration = context.enumeration(idl_type)
    if enumeration is not None:
        return rust_enumeration_path(enumeration, context)
    runtime_type = runtime_union_type(idl_type, context)
    if runtime_type is not None:
        return runtime_type
    optional_member = member_other_than_undefined(idl_type)
    if optional_member is not None:
        return f"Option<{rust_type(optional_member, context, what)}>"
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType):
        for member_type in union_member_types(idl_type, context):
            rust_type(member_type, context, what, is_result)
        return rust_union_path(idl_type, context, what)
    raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has the type {idl_type}, which the Rust bindings do not convert yet")


def is_promise_type(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
    return isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType) and idl_type.name == "Promise"


def holds_cells(
    idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext, enclosing_dictionary_names: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset()
) -> bool:
    """Whether the Rust type of the IDL values of the type is or can hold a cell, which a Vec would hide from the
    collector. Only plain data, and what is made of nothing but plain data, holds none: a type that this function
    does not know holds one."""

    def any_holds_cells(idl_types: Iterable[IDLType]) -> bool:
        return any(holds_cells(inner_type, context, enclosing_dictionary_names) for inner_type in idl_types)

    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType):
        if runtime_union_type(idl_type, context) is not None:
            # NB: The bindings runtime defines the types of its unions by hand, so nothing checks them against the
            #     members of the unions.
            return True
        return any_holds_cells(idl_type.flattened_member_types())
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType):
        if idl_type.name in ("sequence", "FrozenArray", "record"):
            return any_holds_cells(idl_type.parameters)
        return True
    if idl_type.name in PLAIN_DATA_TYPES or context.enumeration(idl_type) is not None:
        return False
    dictionary = resolved_dictionary(idl_type, context)
    if dictionary is None:
        return True
    if dictionary.name in enclosing_dictionary_names:
        # NB: A dictionary that names itself, as it can through a sequence, holds a cell only if a member outside of
        #     that cycle does.
        return False
    return any(
        holds_cells(member.type, context, enclosing_dictionary_names | {dictionary.name})
        for inherited_dictionary in context.dictionary_inheritance_stack(dictionary)
        for member in inherited_dictionary.members
    )


def is_sequence_of_cells(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    """Whether the type is a sequence whose elements are or can hold cells, which the bindings gather in a MarkedVec
    for a parameter."""
    return (
        isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType)
        and idl_type.name == "sequence"
        and not idl_type.nullable
        and holds_cells(idl_type.parameters[0], context)
    )


def is_record_of_cells(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    """Whether the type is a record whose values are or can hold cells, which the bindings gather in a MarkedVec for a
    parameter."""
    return (
        isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType)
        and idl_type.name == "record"
        and not idl_type.nullable
        and holds_cells(idl_type.parameters[1], context)
    )


def union_holds_sequence_of_cells(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    """Whether the type is a union with a member that is a sequence of values that are or can hold cells, which the
    enum of the union keeps alive in a MarkedVec, for as long as the reference to the VM that it was converted with
    lives."""
    return isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType) and any(
        is_sequence_of_cells(member_type, context) for member_type in idl_type.flattened_member_types()
    )


def dictionary_holds_sequence_of_cells(dictionary: Dictionary, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    """Whether a member of the dictionary is a sequence of values that are or can hold cells, or a union with such a
    member, which the struct of the dictionary keeps alive in a MarkedVec, for as long as the reference to the VM that
    it was converted with lives."""
    return any(
        is_sequence_of_cells(member.type, context) or union_holds_sequence_of_cells(member.type, context)
        for member in dictionary.members
    )


def rust_dictionary_type(dictionary: Dictionary, context: GenerationContext) -> str:
    """The Rust type of the struct of a dictionary: its path, with the lifetime of the reference to the VM when the
    dictionary holds a sequence of values that are or can hold cells."""
    path = rust_dictionary_path(dictionary, context)
    if dictionary_holds_sequence_of_cells(dictionary, context):
        return f"{path}<'_>"
    return path


def rust_parameter_type(parameter: OperationParameter, context: GenerationContext, what: str) -> str:
    """The Rust type the implementation receives for the parameter."""
    if parameter.variadic:
        element_type = rust_type(parameter.type, context, what)
        if holds_cells(parameter.type, context):
            return f"MarkedVec<'_, {element_type}>"
        return f"Vec<{element_type}>"
    if is_sequence_of_cells(parameter.type, context):
        assert isinstance(parameter.type, IDLParameterizedType)
        value_type = f"MarkedVec<'_, {rust_type(parameter.type.parameters[0], context, what)}>"
    elif is_record_of_cells(parameter.type, context):
        assert isinstance(parameter.type, IDLParameterizedType)
        key_type, record_value_type = (rust_type(type, context, what) for type in parameter.type.parameters)
        value_type = f"MarkedVec<'_, ({key_type}, {record_value_type})>"
    else:
        value_type = rust_type(parameter.type, context, what)
    if parameter.optional and parameter.default_value is None:
        return f"Option<{value_type}>"
    return value_type

# Which language's bindings name which definition. An interface is implemented in one language, but a dictionary is
# data that the bindings of both languages can convert, so it gets a representation in each language that names it,
# wherever its IDL defines it.

from collections.abc import Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict
from typing import List
from typing import Set

from Generators.libweb_bindings.context import GenerationContext
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_members import rust_members
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import cpp_interface
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import inheriting_interfaces
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_implemented_in_rust
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_member_implemented_in_rust
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_named_union
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import runtime_union_type
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_implemented_members
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_interface
from Utils.webidl_parser import Dictionary
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLUnionType
from Utils.webidl_parser import Interface
from Utils.webidl_parser import Module


def types_named_by_interface(interface: Interface, with_unimplemented_members: bool = True) -> List[IDLType]:
    """Every type that the members of the interface name. The bindings of the interface convert them, except those of
    the members marked [FIXME], which they only record as not implemented."""

    def is_wanted(extended_attributes: Dict[str, str]) -> bool:
        return with_unimplemented_members or "FIXME" not in extended_attributes

    types = []
    for attribute in interface.regular_attributes + interface.static_attributes:
        # NB: The Rust bindings convert the values of an attribute marked [ImplementedIn=Rust].
        if is_member_implemented_in_rust(attribute) and not is_implemented_in_rust(interface):
            continue
        if is_wanted(attribute.extended_attributes):
            types.append(attribute.type)
    for operation in interface.regular_operations + interface.static_operations:
        if not is_wanted(operation.extended_attributes):
            continue
        # NB: The Rust bindings convert the values of an operation marked [ImplementedIn=Rust].
        if is_member_implemented_in_rust(operation) and not is_implemented_in_rust(interface):
            continue
        types.append(operation.return_type)
        types.extend(parameter.type for parameter in operation.parameters)
    for constructor in interface.constructors:
        types.extend(parameter.type for parameter in constructor.parameters)
    special_operations = [
        interface.named_property_getter,
        interface.indexed_property_getter,
        interface.named_property_setter,
        interface.indexed_property_setter,
        interface.named_property_deleter,
    ]
    for special_operation in special_operations:
        if special_operation is not None:
            types.append(special_operation.return_type)
            types.extend(parameter.type for parameter in special_operation.parameters)
    if interface.stringifier is not None and interface.stringifier.attribute is not None:
        types.append(interface.stringifier.attribute.type)
    if interface.iterable is not None:
        types.extend([interface.iterable.key_type, interface.iterable.value_type])
    if interface.async_iterable is not None:
        types.extend([interface.async_iterable.key_type, interface.async_iterable.value_type])
        types.extend(parameter.type for parameter in interface.async_iterable.parameters)
    if interface.maplike is not None:
        types.extend([interface.maplike.key_type, interface.maplike.value_type])
    if interface.setlike is not None:
        types.append(interface.setlike.value_type)
    return [idl_type for idl_type in types if idl_type is not None]


@dataclass
class ConversionDirections:
    """The directions in which the Rust bindings convert a definition."""

    from_js: bool = False
    to_js: bool = False


class DefinitionUsage:
    """Raises the errors of rust_members() for the interfaces implemented in Rust, whose members it reads."""

    def __init__(self, context: GenerationContext) -> None:
        self.context = context
        # The dictionaries that the interfaces implemented in Rust name, in the order of their first use.
        self.rust_dictionaries: Dict[str, ConversionDirections] = {}
        # The unions that the interfaces implemented in Rust name and that have an enum of their own, by their type.
        self.rust_unions: Dict[IDLUnionType, ConversionDirections] = {}
        # The enumerations that the interfaces implemented in Rust name.
        self.rust_enumerations: Dict[str, ConversionDirections] = {}
        # The interfaces that LibWeb implements in C++ and that the interfaces implemented in Rust name.
        self.cpp_interfaces_named_by_rust: Dict[str, Interface] = {}
        # The dictionaries that have a C++ representation.
        self.cpp_dictionary_names: Set[str] = set()
        # The interfaces implemented in Rust that the C++ bindings convert objects of, and so need a C++ class for.
        self.rust_interfaces_named_by_cpp: Dict[str, Interface] = {}
        # The interfaces implemented in Rust that others inherit from and that the interfaces implemented in Rust
        # convert JS values to.
        self.rust_any_interfaces: Dict[str, Interface] = {}
        self._collect_rust_dictionaries()
        self._collect_cpp_dictionaries()
        self._collect_rust_interfaces_named_by_cpp()

    def cpp_dictionaries(self, module: Module) -> List[Dictionary]:
        """The dictionaries of the module that the C++ bindings declare and convert."""
        return [dictionary for dictionary in module.dictionaries if dictionary.name in self.cpp_dictionary_names]

    def _collect_rust_dictionaries(self) -> None:
        # NB: An implementation in Rust converts JS values to a dictionary marked [ImplementedIn=Rust] itself, as the
        #     constructor of ReadableStream converts its underlyingSource object to an UnderlyingSource.
        for dictionary in self.context.dictionaries.values():
            if dictionary.extended_attributes.get("ImplementedIn") == "Rust":
                self._name_for_rust(IDLType(dictionary.name), from_js=True, to_js=False)
        for module in self.context.modules:
            interface = module.interface
            rust_members_of_cpp_interface = rust_implemented_members(interface)
            if rust_members_of_cpp_interface is not None:
                assert interface is not None
                # NB: The bindings of the members check that their this value implements the interface.
                self.cpp_interfaces_named_by_rust[interface.name] = interface
                self._name_members_for_rust(rust_members_of_cpp_interface)
                continue
            if interface is None or not is_implemented_in_rust(interface):
                continue
            parent = self.context.interfaces.get(interface.parent_name)
            if parent is not None and not is_implemented_in_rust(parent):
                # NB: The bindings of the interface name the interface implemented in C++ it inherits from, whose
                #     interface prototype object and interface object are the prototypes of its own.
                self.cpp_interfaces_named_by_rust[parent.name] = parent
            self._name_members_for_rust(interface)

    def _name_members_for_rust(self, interface: Interface) -> None:
        members = rust_members(interface)
        for attribute in members.attributes:
            if attribute.event_type is not None:
                continue
            has_setter = attribute.setter_method is not None
            self._name_for_rust(attribute.attribute.type, from_js=has_setter, to_js=True)
        operations = [
            overload.operation
            for operation_set in members.operation_sets + members.static_operation_sets
            for overload in operation_set.overloads
        ]
        if members.indexed_property_getter is not None:
            operations.append(members.indexed_property_getter.operation.operation)
        if members.indexed_property_setter is not None:
            self._name_for_rust(members.indexed_property_setter.value_parameter.type, from_js=True, to_js=False)
        for operation in operations:
            self._name_for_rust(operation.return_type, from_js=False, to_js=True)
            for parameter in operation.parameters:
                self._name_for_rust(parameter.type, from_js=True, to_js=False)
        for constructor in members.constructors:
            for parameter in constructor.constructor.parameters:
                self._name_for_rust(parameter.type, from_js=True, to_js=False)
        if members.async_iterator is not None:
            for parameter in members.async_iterator.parameters:
                self._name_for_rust(parameter.type, from_js=True, to_js=False)

    def _name_for_rust(self, idl_type: IDLType, from_js: bool, to_js: bool) -> None:
        if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType):
            # NB: The bindings runtime converts the unions that it has a type for as a whole.
            if runtime_union_type(idl_type, self.context) is not None:
                return
            if is_named_union(idl_type, self.context):
                union_type = idl_type.without_nullable()
                assert isinstance(union_type, IDLUnionType)
                directions = self.rust_unions.setdefault(union_type, ConversionDirections())
                directions.from_js = directions.from_js or from_js
                directions.to_js = directions.to_js or to_js
            for member_type in idl_type.flattened_member_types():
                self._name_for_rust(member_type, from_js, to_js)
            return
        for child_type in idl_type.child_types():
            self._name_for_rust(child_type, from_js, to_js)
        named_cpp_interface = cpp_interface(idl_type, self.context)
        if named_cpp_interface is not None:
            self.cpp_interfaces_named_by_rust[named_cpp_interface.name] = named_cpp_interface
            return
        named_rust_interface = rust_interface(idl_type, self.context)
        if named_rust_interface is not None:
            if from_js and inheriting_interfaces(named_rust_interface, self.context):
                self.rust_any_interfaces[named_rust_interface.name] = named_rust_interface
            return
        if idl_type.name in self.context.enumerations:
            directions = self.rust_enumerations.setdefault(idl_type.name, ConversionDirections())
            directions.from_js = directions.from_js or from_js
            directions.to_js = directions.to_js or to_js
            return
        dictionary = self.context.dictionaries.get(idl_type.name)
        if dictionary is None:
            return
        from_js = from_js or "GenerateFromJSON" in dictionary.extended_attributes
        to_js = to_js or "GenerateToValue" in dictionary.extended_attributes
        directions = self.rust_dictionaries.setdefault(dictionary.name, ConversionDirections())
        if (directions.from_js or not from_js) and (directions.to_js or not to_js):
            return
        directions.from_js = directions.from_js or from_js
        directions.to_js = directions.to_js or to_js
        for member in self._members_with_inherited(dictionary):
            self._name_for_rust(member.type, from_js, to_js)
        if dictionary.parent_name:
            # NB: The conversion of a dictionary converts the dictionary that it inherits from first.
            self._name_for_rust(IDLType(dictionary.parent_name), from_js, to_js)

    def _members_with_inherited(self, dictionary: Dictionary):
        members = list(dictionary.members)
        parent = self.context.dictionaries.get(dictionary.parent_name) if dictionary.parent_name else None
        if parent is not None:
            members.extend(self._members_with_inherited(parent))
        return members

    def _collect_cpp_dictionaries(self) -> None:
        for module in self.context.modules:
            if is_implemented_in_rust(module.interface):
                continue
            # NB: The C++ bindings declare and convert every dictionary of the modules that they generate, whether
            #     or not an interface names it, unless only the Rust bindings convert JS values to it.
            for dictionary in module.dictionaries:
                directions = self.rust_dictionaries.get(dictionary.name)
                if directions is None or not directions.from_js:
                    self._name_for_cpp(dictionary.name)
            self._name_types_for_cpp(self.types_named_by_cpp_module(module))

    def _collect_rust_interfaces_named_by_cpp(self) -> None:
        def name(types: Iterable[IDLType]) -> None:
            for idl_type in types:
                for nested_type in idl_type.nested_types():
                    interface = self.context.interfaces.get(nested_type.name)
                    if is_implemented_in_rust(interface):
                        assert interface is not None
                        self.rust_interfaces_named_by_cpp[interface.name] = interface

        for module in self.context.modules:
            if not is_implemented_in_rust(module.interface):
                name(self.types_named_by_cpp_module(module, with_unimplemented_members=False))
            for dictionary in self.cpp_dictionaries(module):
                name(member.type for member in dictionary.members)

    def types_named_by_cpp_module(self, module: Module, with_unimplemented_members: bool = True) -> List[IDLType]:
        """The types that the interface, typedefs and callback functions of a module of the C++ bindings name."""
        types = []
        if module.interface is not None:
            types.extend(types_named_by_interface(module.interface, with_unimplemented_members))
        types.extend(typedef.type for typedef in module.typedefs)
        for callback_function in module.callback_functions:
            types.append(callback_function.return_type)
            types.extend(parameter.type for parameter in callback_function.parameters)
        return types

    def _name_types_for_cpp(self, types: Iterable[IDLType]) -> None:
        for idl_type in types:
            for nested_type in idl_type.nested_types():
                if nested_type.name in self.context.dictionaries:
                    self._name_for_cpp(nested_type.name)

    def _name_for_cpp(self, name: str) -> None:
        if name in self.cpp_dictionary_names:
            return
        self.cpp_dictionary_names.add(name)
        dictionary = self.context.dictionaries[name]
        if dictionary.parent_name in self.context.dictionaries:
            self._name_for_cpp(dictionary.parent_name)
        self._name_types_for_cpp(member.type for member in dictionary.members)

from typing import Literal
from typing import Optional

from Generators.libweb_bindings.context import GenerationContext
from Generators.libweb_bindings.includes import GeneratedIncludes
from Utils.webidl_parser import Interface

SecurityCheckType = Literal["method", "getter", "setter"]


def interface_needs_security_check(context: GenerationContext, interface: Interface) -> bool:
    # NB: Only a Window or Location object can fail the security check, so other interfaces' impl_from() performs it
    #     only once their implementation check fails.
    for platform_interface_name in ("Window", "Location"):
        platform_interface = context.interfaces.get(platform_interface_name)
        if platform_interface is None:
            continue
        if any(
            interface_in_chain.name == interface.name
            for interface_in_chain in context.inheritance_stack(platform_interface)
        ):
            return True
    return False


# https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-check-an-object
def implementation_check(js_value: Optional[str], identifier: str, type_: SecurityCheckType) -> str:
    js_value_argument = f"{js_value}, " if js_value else ""
    return f'impl_from(vm, {js_value_argument}u"{identifier}"sv, HTML::SecurityCheckType::{type_.capitalize()})'


# https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-perform-a-security-check
def perform_a_security_check(
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    js_value: str,
    identifier: str,
    type_: SecurityCheckType,
) -> str:
    includes.add("LibWeb/HTML/CrossOrigin/AbstractOperations.h")
    return f'TRY(HTML::perform_a_security_check(vm, {js_value}, u"{identifier}"sv, HTML::SecurityCheckType::{type_.capitalize()}));'


# https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#crossoriginproperties-(-o-)
# CrossOriginProperties(O) for a Window object O, as [[NeedsGet]] and [[NeedsSet]], or None for an operation.
CROSS_ORIGIN_WINDOW_PROPERTIES: dict[str, Optional[tuple[bool, bool]]] = {
    "window": (True, False),
    "self": (True, False),
    "location": (True, True),
    "close": None,
    "closed": (True, False),
    "focus": None,
    "blur": None,
    "frames": (True, False),
    "length": (True, False),
    "top": (True, False),
    "opener": (True, False),
    "parent": (True, False),
    "postMessage": None,
}


def window_member_is_cross_origin_accessible(interface: Interface, identifier: str, type_: SecurityCheckType) -> bool:
    if interface.name != "Window" or identifier not in CROSS_ORIGIN_WINDOW_PROPERTIES:
        return False
    entry = CROSS_ORIGIN_WINDOW_PROPERTIES[identifier]
    if type_ == "method":
        return entry is None
    if type_ == "getter":
        return entry is not None and entry[0]
    return entry is not None and entry[1]


def the_remote_window(includes: GeneratedIncludes, js_value: str) -> str:
    # NOTE: A WindowProxy's [[Window]] may be a RemoteWindow standing for a Window hosted by another process. The
    #       security check only lets a cross-origin accessible member through for it, and RemoteWindow declares that
    #       member as Window does, so the steps below run on whichever of the two jsValue's [[Window]] is.
    includes.add("LibWeb/HTML/CrossOrigin/AbstractOperations.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/HTML/RemoteWindow.h")
    return f"auto remote_window = HTML::remote_window_from({js_value});"


def on_the_window(call: str) -> str:
    return f"HTML::invoke_on_window(idl_object, remote_window.ptr(), [&](auto& window) {{ return {call}; }})"

from Utils.webidl_parser import Dictionary
from Utils.webidl_parser import Enumeration
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLParameterizedType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLUnionType
from Utils.webidl_parser import Interface


@dataclass
class UnionTypes:
    boolean_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    numeric_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    string_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    bigint_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    array_buffer_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    data_view_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    sequence_type: Optional[IDLParameterizedType] = None
    frozen_array_type: Optional[IDLParameterizedType] = None
    record_type: Optional[IDLParameterizedType] = None
    dictionary_type: Optional[IDLType] = None

    enumeration_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)
    interface_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)
    callback_function_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)
    callback_interface_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)
    typed_array_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)

    includes_object_type: bool = False


def collect_union_types(flattened_member_types: List[IDLType], context: GenerationContext) -> UnionTypes:
    types = UnionTypes()

    for member_type in flattened_member_types:
        if types.boolean_type is None and member_type.name == "boolean":
            types.boolean_type = member_type
        if types.numeric_type is None and is_numeric_type(member_type.name):
            types.numeric_type = member_type
        if types.string_type is None and is_string_type(member_type.name):
            types.string_type = member_type
        if types.bigint_type is None and member_type.name == "bigint":
            types.bigint_type = member_type

        if context.enumeration(member_type) is not None:
            types.enumeration_types.append(member_type)
        if interface_like_type_for_idl_type(member_type, context) is not None:
            types.interface_types.append(member_type)
        if context.callback_function(member_type) is not None:
            types.callback_function_types.append(member_type)

        interface = context.interface(member_type)
        if interface is not None and interface.is_callback_interface:
            types.callback_interface_types.append(member_type)

        if member_type.name == "object":
            types.includes_object_type = True
        if types.array_buffer_type is None and member_type.name == "ArrayBuffer":
            types.array_buffer_type = member_type
        if types.data_view_type is None and member_type.name == "DataView":
            types.data_view_type = member_type
        if is_typed_array_type(member_type):
            types.typed_array_types.append(member_type)
        if types.dictionary_type is None and context.dictionary(member_type) is not None:
            types.dictionary_type = member_type

        if not isinstance(member_type, IDLParameterizedType):
            continue

        if types.sequence_type is None and member_type.name == "sequence":
            types.sequence_type = member_type
        if types.frozen_array_type is None and member_type.name == "FrozenArray":
            types.frozen_array_type = member_type
        if types.record_type is None and member_type.name == "record":
            types.record_type = member_type

    return types


def unsupported_to_idl_value(idl_type: IDLType) -> str:
    raise RuntimeError(f"Unsupported IDL value conversion for '{idl_type}'")


def idl_value_conversion_is_throwing(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext) -> bool:
    return idl_type.name not in ("any", "boolean")


def write_enumeration_declaration(out: TextIO, enumeration: Enumeration, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> None:
    includes.add("LibJS/Forward.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")

    out.write(
        f"JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{enumeration.name}> {converter_function_name(enumeration)}(JS::VM&, JS::Value);\n\n"
    )


def write_enumeration_definition(out: TextIO, enumeration: Enumeration) -> None:
    out.write(f"enum class {enumeration.name} : {underlying_type_for_enum(len(enumeration.values))} {{\n")
    for value in enumeration.values:
        out.write(f"    {string_to_cpp_enum_name(value)},\n")
    out.write("};\n\n")


def write_dictionary_declaration(
    out: TextIO,
    dictionary: Dictionary,
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    context: GenerationContext,
) -> None:
    includes.add("LibJS/Forward.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    parent_dictionary = context.dictionary_parent(dictionary)
    if parent_dictionary is not None:
        includes.add_binding(parent_dictionary.path.stem)

    parent = f" : public {dictionary.parent_name}" if dictionary.parent_name else ""
    out.write(f"struct {dictionary.name}{parent} {{\n")
    for member in dictionary.members:
        add_header_includes_for_type(member, includes, context)

        default_value = ""
        if member.default_value is not None:
            default_value = f" {cpp_default_value_conversion(member, context)} "
        member_cpp_type = cpp_type(member, context)
        if member.required and member.default_value is None:
            out.write(f"    {member_cpp_type} {cpp_name(member)};\n")
        else:
            out.write(f"    {member_cpp_type} {cpp_name(member)} {{{default_value}}};\n")

    # NB: A dictionary is traced through its members, so that a GC::Function can capture it.
    includes.add("LibGC/CaptureTraits.h")
    if dictionary.members or dictionary.parent_name:
        out.write("\n    void visit_edges(auto& visitor) const\n    {\n")
        if dictionary.parent_name:
            out.write(f"        {dictionary.parent_name}::visit_edges(visitor);\n")
        for member in dictionary.members:
            out.write(f"        GC::visit_capture_member(visitor, {cpp_name(member)});\n")
        out.write("    }\n")
    else:
        out.write("\n    void visit_edges(auto&) const { }\n")
    out.write("};\n\n")
    out.write(
        f"JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{dictionary.name}> {converter_function_name(dictionary)}(JS::VM&, JS::Value);\n\n"
    )


def dictionaries_in_dependency_order(dictionaries: List[Dictionary], context: GenerationContext) -> List[Dictionary]:
    local_dictionaries = {dictionary.name: dictionary for dictionary in dictionaries}
    emitted: set[str] = set()
    visiting: set[str] = set()
    ordered_dictionaries: List[Dictionary] = []

    def dependency_names_for(dictionary: Dictionary) -> List[str]:
        dependency_names = {dictionary.parent_name} if dictionary.parent_name else set()
        for member in dictionary.members:
            dependency_names.update(context.dictionary_type_names(member.type))
        dependency_names.discard(dictionary.name)
        return sorted(dependency_names)

    def visit(dictionary: Dictionary) -> None:
        if dictionary.name in emitted:
            return
        if dictionary.name in visiting:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Dictionary '{dictionary.name}' depends on itself")

        visiting.add(dictionary.name)
        for dependency_name in dependency_names_for(dictionary):
            dependency = local_dictionaries.get(dependency_name)
            if dependency is not None:
                visit(dependency)
        visiting.remove(dictionary.name)

        ordered_dictionaries.append(dictionary)
        emitted.add(dictionary.name)

    for dictionary in local_dictionaries.values():
        visit(dictionary)

    return ordered_dictionaries


def write_enumeration_conversion(out: TextIO, enumeration: Enumeration, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> None:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Error.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/VM.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")

    out.write(
        f"""// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-enumeration
JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{enumeration.name}> {converter_function_name(enumeration)}(JS::VM& vm, JS::Value value)
{{
    // 1. Let S be the result of calling ? ToString(V).
    auto value_as_string = TRY(value.to_utf16_string(vm));

    // 2. If S is not one of E’s enumeration values, then throw a TypeError.
    // 3. Return the enumeration value of type E that is equal to S.
"""
    )

    for value in enumeration.values:
        out.write(f'    if (value_as_string == "{value}"sv)\n')
        out.write(f"        return {enumeration.name}::{string_to_cpp_enum_name(value)};\n")
    out.write(
        f"""    return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::InvalidEnumerationValue, value_as_string, "{enumeration.name}");
}}

"""
    )


def write_dictionary_conversion(
    out: TextIO,
    dictionary: Dictionary,
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    context: GenerationContext,
) -> None:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Error.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/VM.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/WebIDL/ExceptionOrUtils.h")

    parent_dictionary = context.dictionary_parent(dictionary)

    out.write(f"""// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-dictionary
JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{dictionary.name}> {converter_function_name(dictionary)}(JS::VM& vm, JS::Value js_dict)
{{
    // 1. If jsDict is not an Object and jsDict is neither undefined nor null, then throw a TypeError.
    if (!js_dict.is_object() && !js_dict.is_nullish())
        return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, "{dictionary.name}");

    // 2. Let idlDict be an empty ordered map, representing a dictionary of type D.
    // 3. Let dictionaries be a list consisting of D and all of D’s inherited dictionaries, in order from least to most derived.
    // 4. For each dictionary dictionary in dictionaries, in order:
    // NB: We defer construction until the return initializer because some members may not be default-constructible. Inherited dictionaries are represented by the generated C++ struct inheritance.

    // 5. Return idlDict.
    return {dictionary.name} {{
""")
    if parent_dictionary is not None:
        out.write(f"        TRY({converter_function_name(parent_dictionary)}(vm, js_dict)),\n")

    # 4.1. For each dictionary member member declared on dictionary, in lexicographical order:
    for member in dictionary.members:
        conversion = to_idl_value(member, "js_member_value", includes, context)
        member_cpp_type = cpp_type(member, context)
        member_designator = "" if parent_dictionary is not None else f".{cpp_name(member)} = "
        out.write(
            f"""        {member_designator}TRY([&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{member_cpp_type}> {{
            // 1. Let key be the identifier of member.
            {static_utf16_fly_string("key", member.name)}

            // 2. If jsDict is either undefined or null, then:
            //     1. Let jsMemberValue be undefined.
            // 3. Otherwise,
            //     1. Let jsMemberValue be ? Get(jsDict, key).
            auto js_member_value = JS::js_undefined();
            if (js_dict.is_object())
                js_member_value = TRY(js_dict.as_object().get(key));

            // 4. If jsMemberValue is not undefined, then:
            if (!js_member_value.is_undefined()) {{
                // 1. Let idlMemberValue be the result of converting jsMemberValue to an IDL value whose type is the type member is declared to be of.
                auto idl_member_value = TRY(WebIDL::throw_dom_exception_if_needed(vm, *vm.current_realm(), [&] {{ return {conversion}; }}));

                // 2. Set idlDict[key] to idlMemberValue.
                return idl_member_value;
            }}
"""
        )
        if member.default_value is not None:
            out.write(
                f"""            // 5. Otherwise, if jsMemberValue is undefined but member has a default value, then:
            // 1. Let idlMemberValue be the result of converting member's default value to an IDL value whose type is the type member is declared to be of.
            auto idl_member_value = {cpp_default_value_conversion(member, context)};

            // 2. Set idlDict[key] to idlMemberValue.
            return idl_member_value;
"""
            )
        elif member.required:
            out.write(
                f"""            // 6. Otherwise, if jsMemberValue is undefined and member is required, then throw a TypeError.
            return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::MissingRequiredProperty, "{member.name}");
"""
            )
        else:
            out.write(
                f"""            // 7. Otherwise, jsMemberValue is undefined and the member is optional.
            return {cpp_empty_value(member, context)};
"""
            )

        out.write("        }()),\n")
    out.write(
        """    };
}

"""
    )


# 3.2.1. any, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-any
def any_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")

    # 1. If V is undefined, then return the unique undefined IDL value.
    # 2. If V is null, then return the null object? reference.
    # 3. If V is a Boolean, then return the boolean value that represents the same truth value.
    # 4. If V is a Number, then return the result of converting V to an unrestricted double.
    # 5. If V is a BigInt, then return the result of converting V to a bigint.
    # 6. If V is a String, then return the result of converting V to a DOMString.
    # 7. If V is a Symbol, then return the result of converting V to a symbol.
    # 8. If V is an Object, then return an IDL object value that references V.
    # NB: We're getting passed a JS::Value - which is already our C++ representation, so we can just return it as-is.
    return value_name


# 3.2.3. boolean, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-boolean
def boolean_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")

    # 1. Let x be the result of computing ToBoolean(V).
    # 2. Return the IDL boolean value that is the one that represents the same truth value as the JavaScript Boolean value x.
    return f"{value_name}.to_boolean()"


# https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-converttoint
def convert_to_int(
    cpp_type: str,
    value_name: str,
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    extended_attributes: dict[str, str],
) -> str:
    includes.add("LibWebCommon/WebIDL/Types.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/WebIDL/AbstractOperations.h")

    enforce_range = "Yes" if "EnforceRange" in extended_attributes else "No"
    clamp = "Yes" if "Clamp" in extended_attributes else "No"
    return (
        f"WebIDL::convert_to_int<{cpp_type}>(vm, {value_name}, "
        f"WebIDL::EnforceRange::{enforce_range}, WebIDL::Clamp::{clamp})"
    )


# 3.2.4.1. byte, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-byte
def byte_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes, extended_attributes: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    # 1. Let x be ? ConvertToInt(V, 8, "signed").
    # 2. Return the IDL byte value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    return convert_to_int("WebIDL::Byte", value_name, includes, extended_attributes)


# 3.2.4.2. octet, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-octet
def octet_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes, extended_attributes: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    # 1. Let x be ? ConvertToInt(V, 8, "unsigned").
    # 2. Return the IDL octet value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    return convert_to_int("WebIDL::Octet", value_name, includes, extended_attributes)

# 3.2.5. float, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-float
def float_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes, identifier: str) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Error.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")

    # 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    # 2. If x is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then throw a TypeError.
    # 3. Let S be the set of finite IEEE 754 single-precision floating point values except −0, but with two special values added: 2^128 and −2^128.
    # 4. Let y be the number in S that is closest to x, selecting the number with an even significand if there are two equally close values. (The two special values 2^128 and −2^128 are considered to have even significands for this purpose.)
    # 5. If y is 2^128 or −2^128, then throw a TypeError.
    # 6. If y is +0 and x is negative, return −0.
    # 7. Return y.
    # FIXME: Correctly implement steps 3-7.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<float> {{
        float x = TRY({value_name}.to_double(vm));
        if (isinf(x) || isnan(x))
            return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::InvalidRestrictedFloatingPointParameter, "{identifier}");
        return x;
    }}()"""


# 3.2.6. unrestricted float, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unrestricted-float
def unrestricted_float_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")

    # 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    # 2. If x is NaN, then return the IDL unrestricted float value that represents the IEEE 754 NaN value with the bit pattern 0x7fc00000 [IEEE-754].
    # 3. Let S be the set of finite IEEE 754 single-precision floating point values except −0, but with two special values added: 2^128 and −2^128.
    # 4. Let y be the number in S that is closest to x, selecting the number with an even significand if there are two equally close values. (The two special values 2^128 and −2^128 are considered to have even significands for this purpose.)
    # 5. If y is 2^128, return +∞.
    # 6. If y is −2^128, return −∞.
    # 7. If y is +0 and x is negative, return −0.
    # 8. Return y.
    # FIXME: Correctly implement steps 2-8.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<float> {{
        return static_cast<float>(TRY({value_name}.to_double(vm)));
    }}()"""


# 3.2.7. double, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-double
def double_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes, identifier: str) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Error.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")

    # 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    # 2. If x is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then throw a TypeError.
    # 3. Return the IDL double value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<double> {{
        auto x = TRY({value_name}.to_double(vm));
        if (isinf(x) || isnan(x))
            return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::InvalidRestrictedFloatingPointParameter, "{identifier}");
        return x;
    }}()"""


# 3.2.8. unrestricted double, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unrestricted-double
def unrestricted_double_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")
    # 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    # 2. If x is NaN, then return the IDL unrestricted double value that represents the IEEE 754 NaN value with the bit pattern 0x7ff8000000000000 [IEEE-754].
    # 3. Return the IDL unrestricted double value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    # FIXME!
    return f"{value_name}.to_double(vm)"

# 3.2.10. DOMString, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-DOMString
def dom_string_to_idl_value(
    value_name: str,
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    extended_attributes: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None,
    type_name: str = "DOMString",
) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/WebIDL/AbstractOperations.h")
    cpp_type_name = cpp_type_name_for_string(type_name, extended_attributes)
    add_include_for_string_cpp_type(cpp_type_name, includes)

    # 1. If V is null and the conversion is to an IDL type associated with the [LegacyNullToEmptyString] extended attribute, then return the DOMString value that represents the empty string.
    if extended_attributes is not None and "LegacyNullToEmptyString" in extended_attributes:
        return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{cpp_type_name}> {{
        {cpp_type_name} string;
        if (!{value_name}.is_null())
            string = TRY(WebIDL::to_utf16_string(vm, {value_name}));
        return string;
    }}()"""
    # 2. Let x be ? ToString(V).
    # 3. Return the IDL DOMString value that represents the same sequence of code units as the one the JavaScript String value x represents.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{cpp_type_name}> {{
        return TRY(WebIDL::to_utf16_string(vm, {value_name}));
    }}()"""


# 3.2.11. ByteString, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-ByteString
def bytestring_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/WebIDL/AbstractOperations.h")
    cpp_type_name = cpp_type_name_for_string("ByteString")
    add_include_for_string_cpp_type(cpp_type_name, includes)
    # 1. Let x be ? ToString(V).
    # 2. If the value of any element of x is greater than 255, then throw a TypeError.
    # 3. Return an IDL ByteString value whose length is the length of x, and where the value of each element is the value of the corresponding element of x.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{cpp_type_name}> {{
        return TRY(WebIDL::to_byte_string(vm, {value_name}));
    }}()"""


# 3.2.12. USVString, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-USVString
def usv_string_to_idl_value(
    value_name: str,
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    extended_attributes: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None,
    type_name: str = "USVString",
) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/WebIDL/AbstractOperations.h")
    cpp_type_name = cpp_type_name_for_string(type_name, extended_attributes)
    add_include_for_string_cpp_type(cpp_type_name, includes)

    # 1. Let string be the result of converting V to a DOMString.
    # 2. If x contains any lone surrogates, then throw a TypeError.
    # 3. Return the IDL USVString value that represents the same sequence of code units as the one the JavaScript String value x represents.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<{cpp_type_name}> {{
        return TRY(WebIDL::to_utf16_usv_string(vm, {value_name}));
    }}()"""


# 3.2.13. object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-object
def object_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Error.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Object.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")
    # 1. If V is not an Object, then throw a TypeError.
    # 2. Return the IDL object value that is a reference to the same object as V.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<JS::Object>> {{
        if (!{value_name}.is_object())
            return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObject, {value_name});
        return GC::Ref {{ {value_name}.as_object() }};
    }}()"""

def symbol_to_idl_value(value_name: str, includes: GeneratedIncludes) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    # 1. If V is not a Symbol, then throw a TypeError.
    # 2. Return the result of converting V to an IDL symbol value.
    raise RuntimeError("symbol to IDL value conversion is not yet implemented")


# 3.2.15. Interface types, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-interface
def interface_to_idl_value(
    value_name: str,
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    interface_like_type: InterfaceLikeType,
) -> str:
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Error.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")
    includes.add(interface_like_type.implementation_header)
    if interface_like_type.name == "WindowProxy":
        return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<{interface_like_type.fully_qualified_name}>> {{
        if (!{value_name}.is_object())
            return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, "{interface_like_type.name}");

        if (auto* window_proxy = {interface_like_type.fully_qualified_name}::from_object({value_name}.as_object()))
            return GC::Ref {{ *window_proxy }};
        return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, "{interface_like_type.name}");
    }}()"""
    includes.add("LibWeb/Bindings/Wrappable.h")

    # 1. If V implements I, then return the IDL interface type value that represents a reference to that platform object.
    # 2. Throw a TypeError.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<{interface_like_type.fully_qualified_name}>> {{
        if (!{value_name}.is_object())
            return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, "{interface_like_type.name}");

        if (auto* impl = Web::Bindings::impl_from<{interface_like_type.fully_qualified_name}>(&{value_name}.as_object()))
            return GC::Ref {{ *impl }};
        return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, "{interface_like_type.name}");
    }}()"""


# 3.2.16. Callback interface types, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-callback-interface
def callback_interface_to_idl_value(
    value_name: str,
    includes: GeneratedIncludes,
    interface: Interface,
) -> str:
    includes.add("LibGC/Heap.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Error.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/Value.h")
    includes.add("LibJS/Runtime/ValueInlines.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/WebIDL/ExceptionOrUtils.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/HTML/Scripting/Environments.h")
    includes.add("LibWeb/WebIDL/CallbackType.h")
    includes.add(implementation_header_for_interface(interface))

    cpp_type = fully_qualified_name_for_interface(interface)
    # 1. If V is not an Object, then throw a TypeError.
    # 2. Return the IDL callback interface type value that represents a reference to V, with the incumbent settings object as the callback context.
    return f"""[&]() -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<{cpp_type}>> {{
        if (!{value_name}.is_object())
            return vm.throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObject, {value_name});

        auto callback_type = vm.heap().allocate<WebIDL::CallbackType>({value_name}.as_object(), HTML::incumbent_realm());
        return {cpp_type}::create(callback_type);
    }}()"""
